at_a_glance: Phở bò is Vietnam’s best-known noodle soup: clear, fragrant beef broth, soft rice noodles, and thin slices of beef finished with herbs. It feels light, comforting, and deeply satisfying.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | sliced beef | herbs | lime
good_to_know: Herbs, lime, chili, and bean sprouts usually arrive on the side. Add them little by little so the broth stays balanced.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở bò.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of beef noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh baw
what_it_is: Phở bò is beef noodle soup with clear, fragrant broth, flat rice noodles, thin slices of beef, onion, herbs, and lime. The best bowls taste clean first, then deepen with beef sweetness and warm spice.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth first, then add herbs, lime, bean sprouts, or chili a little at a time. Keep the seasoning balanced so the broth still leads.
how_locals_order: A simple phở bò order usually gets you the classic beef bowl, but shops may ask which cut you want. If you are unsure, rare beef tastes brighter, while well-done beef feels more familiar.
worth_knowing: Phở is one of Vietnam’s signature noodle soups, with northern and southern styles differing in broth sweetness, herb plates, and condiments.

at_a_glance: A gentler cousin of beef phở, with clear chicken broth, rice noodles, herbs, lime, and tender slices or shreds of gà.
usually_includes: broth | rice noodles | chicken | herbs | lime
good_to_know: Ask for không cay if you do not want chili sauce added.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of chicken noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh gah
what_it_is: Phở gà is chicken noodle soup built on a clean, fragrant broth rather than the deeper beef bones of phở bò. Expect flat rice noodles, chicken, onion, scallion, herbs, and lime or chili on the side.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth before adding anything. Then use lime, herbs, and chili in small steps so you can notice the sweetness of the chicken broth.
how_locals_order: Order Phở gà when you want the cleaner chicken version of phở. Taste the broth before lime or chili, then add herbs gently so the chicken sweetness still comes through.
worth_knowing: Phở gà is a comforting breakfast or light dinner, and in Hanoi especially it can be beautifully spare: broth, noodles, chicken, and herbs with no need for theatrics.

at_a_glance: Phở tái is beef phở with very thin rare beef slices that finish cooking in the hot broth. It is clean, aromatic, and more tender than the well-done beef version.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | rare beef | onion | herbs and lime
good_to_know: If rare beef makes you nervous, order phở chín instead. The broth should still be hot enough to soften the beef at the table.
common_options: well-done beef | extra herbs | bean sprouts | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở tái.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of pho with rare beef.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh tie
what_it_is: Phở tái is beef phở with thin rare beef slices added just before serving, so the hot broth finishes them in the bowl. It gives you tender beef without making the soup heavy.
how_to_enjoy: Let the beef sit in the broth for a moment, then taste before adding chili or lime. Choose phở chín if you want fully cooked beef from the start.
how_locals_order: Phở tái is the order when you want rare beef, so say the full name instead of just phở. Add lime, herbs, and chili after tasting the beef broth; ask chín if you decide you want cooked meat instead.
worth_knowing: Tái means rare or lightly cooked. In a hot bowl of phở, the beef finishes cooking at the table, which is why locals order it confidently.

at_a_glance: Phở chín is beef phở with cooked beef slices, rice noodles, herbs, and clear fragrant broth. It is the safer choice if you want phở without rare meat.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | well-done beef | onion | herbs and lime
good_to_know: Chín means cooked or well-done here. You still season the bowl at the table with herbs, lime, bean sprouts, or chili.
common_options: rare beef | extra herbs | bean sprouts | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở chín.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of pho with well-done beef.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh chin
what_it_is: Phở chín is beef phở with cooked beef slices, clear broth, rice noodles, onion, herbs, and lime. It keeps the classic phở flavor while avoiding rare meat.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth first, then add herbs, lime, bean sprouts, or chili little by little. The cooked beef is already ready to eat.
how_locals_order: Phở chín is the safer phở order when you want well-done beef from the start. Taste the broth first, then add herbs or lime; ask không cay before chili oil or sliced chilies go in.
worth_knowing: Chín means cooked or well-done. Learning chín helps you order phở in Vietnam without accidentally getting rare beef.

english_translation: Pho with rare beef and brisket
at_a_glance: Phở tái nạm gives you two beef textures in one bowl: tender rare beef and richer brisket. It is still a clean broth dish, but the meat feels fuller than plain phở tái.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | rare beef | brisket | herbs and lime
good_to_know: Nạm is brisket, so this bowl has more chew and beef depth. Taste the broth before adding chili sauce or lime.
common_options: extra brisket | extra herbs | bean sprouts | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở tái nạm.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of pho with rare beef and brisket.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh tie nahm
what_it_is: Phở tái nạm combines rare beef with brisket in the same bowl. The rare beef stays tender, while nạm brings a deeper beef flavor and more chew.
how_to_enjoy: Taste both beef cuts before changing the broth. Add lime or chili only after you know how rich the brisket makes the bowl.
how_locals_order: Phở tái nạm is the order when you want rare beef, so say the full name instead of just phở. Add lime, herbs, and chili after tasting the beef broth; ask chín if you decide you want cooked meat instead.
worth_knowing: Tái nạm combines rare beef with brisket or flank, a classic phở-shop move for people who want both tenderness and deeper beef flavor.

at_a_glance: Phở bò viên is beef phở with springy beef meatballs, clear broth, rice noodles, herbs, and lime. It is a good choice when you want texture without rare slices.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | beef meatballs | onion | herbs and lime
good_to_know: Bò viên are bouncy beef meatballs. The texture is firmer than sliced beef and easy to recognize in a mixed phở menu.
common_options: extra meatballs | extra herbs | bean sprouts | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở bò viên.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of pho with beef meatballs.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh baw vee-en
what_it_is: Phở bò viên is phở with beef meatballs instead of sliced beef. The meatballs are springy and mild, while the broth still carries the phở aroma.
how_to_enjoy: Slice or bite the meatballs with noodles and herbs. Add chili sauce slowly so the beef broth stays clear.
how_locals_order: Say Phở bò viên when the beef meatballs are the part you want, not just a plain beef bowl. Locals season lightly at the table, then use extra herbs or bean sprouts only if the broth still feels too heavy.
worth_knowing: Bò viên appears across Vietnamese noodle shops and street snacks. In phở, it is the easiest beef topping if rare meat makes you nervous.

at_a_glance: Phở đặc biệt is the special combination bowl, usually with several beef cuts such as rare beef, brisket, meatballs, tendon, or tripe depending on the shop.
usually_includes: beef broth | rice noodles | mixed beef cuts | onion | herbs and lime
good_to_know: Đặc biệt means special, not one fixed recipe. Ask what is included if tendon, tripe, or rare beef matters.
common_options: no tripe | no tendon | extra herbs | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở đặc biệt.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of special combination pho.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh fuh dak bee-et
what_it_is: Phở đặc biệt is the house combination phở. It lets a shop show several beef textures in one bowl, from tender slices to chewier cuts.
how_to_enjoy: Taste each beef cut before adding condiments. If you are cautious, ask what meats come in the special bowl before ordering.
how_locals_order: Phở đặc biệt means the combination bowl, so it can include mixed beef cuts such as brisket, tendon, tripe, or meatballs. Ask no tripe or no tendon before ordering if those textures are not for you.
worth_knowing: On Vietnamese menus, đặc biệt usually means the fuller house version. It can be delicious, but it is not always the safest first order for texture-sensitive eaters.
traveler_caution: May include tendon, tripe, meatballs, brisket, and rare beef.

at_a_glance: Bún bò Huế is a bold central-Vietnam noodle soup with lemongrass, chili warmth, beef, and thick round noodles. It is richer and spicier than phở.
usually_includes: broth | rice vermicelli | beef | herbs | lime
good_to_know: Ask for less spicy if you are heat-sensitive. The broth is the point, so taste it before adding extra chili.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún bò Huế.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of spicy Hue beef noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon baw hway
what_it_is: Bún bò Huế is a bold central-Vietnam noodle soup with lemongrass, chili warmth, beef, and thicker round noodles. It is richer, deeper, and usually spicier than phở.
how_to_enjoy: Taste before adding chili. If heat is a concern, ask for less spicy early, then use the herbs and lime to brighten the broth.
how_locals_order: For Bún bò Huế, ask ít cay before the bowl is made if you want Hue lemongrass depth without full chili heat. Many diners add herbs and lime, but the red broth should still lead.
worth_knowing: The name points to Huế, the former imperial capital, and the dish is strongly associated with central Vietnam. Recipes still shift by shop, especially the spice level and toppings.
traveler_caution: Ask for less spicy if heat is a concern.

at_a_glance: Bún riêu cua is crab-and-tomato vermicelli soup with a tangy red broth, soft crab mixture, tofu, herbs, and sometimes snails or pork blood cubes. It is bright, savory, and a little rustic.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | crab-tomato broth | tofu | herbs | shrimp paste optional
good_to_know: The sourness usually comes from tomato and tamarind or vinegar-like seasoning, not cream. Ask what toppings are included if you avoid shellfish or pork.
common_options: extra herbs | no shrimp paste | less chili | no pork blood
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún riêu cua.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of crab and tomato noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon ree-ew koo-ah
what_it_is: Bún riêu cua is a crab-and-tomato vermicelli soup with tangy broth, tofu, herbs, and often shrimp paste or extra pork-side toppings. It tastes brighter and more rustic than phở.
how_to_enjoy: Add herbs first, then chili or shrimp paste carefully. The broth already has sour tomato lift, so do not drown it before tasting.
how_locals_order: Order Bún riêu cua for the crab-tomato broth, then decide whether you want the shrimp-paste funk. If mắm tôm worries you, ask for it riêng, on the side, or skip it.
worth_knowing: Bún riêu cua is a northern-rooted tomato and crab noodle soup that many shops personalize with tofu, pork, herbs, and shrimp paste.
traveler_caution: May include shellfish, shrimp paste, pork, snails, or pork blood depending on the shop.

at_a_glance: Bún mắm is a Mekong-style noodle soup with fermented fish broth, rice vermicelli, seafood, pork, eggplant, herbs, and a deep salty aroma. It is bold on purpose.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | fermented fish broth | seafood | pork | eggplant and herbs
good_to_know: This is one of the strongest-flavored soups on a Vietnamese menu. If fermented fish sounds like too much, choose bún riêu or phở first.
common_options: extra herbs | less chili | no pork | ask what seafood
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún mắm.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of fermented fish noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon mahm
what_it_is: Bún mắm is rice vermicelli in fermented fish broth with seafood, pork, eggplant, herbs, and a powerful savory aroma. It is one of the boldest soups in the menu set.
how_to_enjoy: Smell and sip before adding chili. Herbs and vegetables are not decoration; they freshen the fermented fish broth.
how_locals_order: Bún mắm is for people who want the fermented fish broth, so ask what seafood is in today's pot before committing. Less chili and no pork are worth saying early because toppings are added fast.
worth_knowing: Bún mắm is strongly associated with southern and Mekong Delta cooking. The fermented fish base is the identity, not a flaw.
regional_association: southern Vietnam and the Mekong Delta
traveler_caution: Contains fermented fish broth and often seafood or pork.

english_translation: Hanoi chicken, egg, and pork noodle soup
at_a_glance: Bún thang is a delicate Hanoi noodle soup layered with shredded chicken, egg ribbons, pork sausage, herbs, and clear broth. It is refined rather than fiery.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | clear chicken broth | shredded chicken | egg ribbons | pork sausage
good_to_know: The bowl can include pork sausage, egg, and dried-shrimp flavor. It is not just chicken soup.
common_options: extra herbs | less pepper | no pork sausage | ask about shrimp
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún thang.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of Hanoi chicken, egg, and pork noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon tang
what_it_is: Bún thang is a Hanoi soup where thin rice vermicelli sits under careful strips of chicken, egg, pork sausage, herbs, and clear broth.
how_to_enjoy: Keep the first spoonful gentle. Add chili only after tasting the broth, because the pleasure is in the layered clean flavors.
how_locals_order: Bún thang is a delicate Hanoi-style bowl, so locals do not bury it under chili right away. Order it by name and let the chicken, egg ribbons, and pork sausage stay clear and tidy.
worth_knowing: Bún thang is associated with Hanoi cooking and a more delicate soup style than many southern or central bowls.
traveler_caution: May include pork, egg, and dried shrimp.

at_a_glance: Bún mọc is pork-and-mushroom ball noodle soup, usually with rice vermicelli, mọc, pork slices, herbs, and clear broth.
usually_includes: clear pork broth | rice vermicelli | mọc pork-mushroom balls | pork slices | fresh herbs
good_to_know: May contain pork.
common_options: extra herbs | extra mọc | no chili | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún mọc.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of pork meatball noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon mawk
what_it_is: Bún mọc is a clear pork-broth noodle soup featuring mọc: springy pork-and-wood-ear mushroom balls. Rice vermicelli, herbs, lime, and chili let the light broth stay fragrant instead of heavy.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the clear broth first, then add herbs, lime, or chili in small steps. The pleasure is the gentle pork broth against the bouncy mọc balls.
how_locals_order: Order bún mọc when you want a lighter noodle soup rather than a fiery bowl. Ask for extra herbs or no chili before seasoning; many shops expect you to finish the balance at the table.
worth_knowing: Mọc refers to the pork-and-mushroom balls, so this is a useful menu word once you start reading Vietnamese noodle-shop signs.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Bún cá is fish noodle soup, usually with fried or fresh fish, dill or tomato, herbs, and rice vermicelli.
usually_includes: fish broth | rice vermicelli | fried or fresh fish | tomato or dill | fresh herbs
good_to_know: Fish bones can appear, especially in more traditional bowls.
common_options: less spicy | no chili | extra herbs | ask about bones
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún cá.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of fish noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon kah
what_it_is: Bún cá is fish noodle soup, often with fried fish pieces or fresh fish in a bright broth with tomato, dill, herbs, and rice vermicelli. It feels lighter than beef noodle soups but still deeply savory.
how_to_enjoy: Check for bones before your first big bite, then season with lime and chili slowly. Herbs brighten the fish broth, while too much chili can cover the seafood sweetness.
how_locals_order: Order bún cá by the full name and ask có xương không if you are worried about bones. Start with the broth plain, then add herbs, lime, and chili after you understand the shop style.
worth_knowing: Bún cá often feels coastal or northern on a menu, and each city handles the fish differently: crisp fried pieces, softer fillets, tomato brightness, or dill fragrance.

at_a_glance: Bún ốc is snail vermicelli soup, often Hanoi-style, with a tomato-bright broth, herbs, and chewy river snails. It is tangy, clean, and more about texture than richness.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | snails | tomato broth | herbs | chili optional
good_to_know: Ốc means snails. If texture matters, ask before ordering; the snails should be chewy rather than soft like clams.
common_options: extra herbs | less chili | no shrimp paste | ask about snails
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún ốc.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of snail noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon awk
what_it_is: Bún ốc is snail vermicelli soup with a tangy tomato-leaning broth, herbs, and chewy snails. It is a classic example of texture doing as much work as flavor.
how_to_enjoy: Try the snails with broth and herbs before adding extra chili. If chewy seafood textures are not your thing, choose another soup.
how_locals_order: Say Bún ốc when you specifically want snails in a tangy tomato broth. Ask about the snails or request less chili first, then brighten the bowl with herbs once it arrives.
worth_knowing: Bún ốc is especially associated with Hanoi-style street eating, though you may see versions elsewhere.
traveler_caution: Contains snails and may include shrimp paste.

at_a_glance: Bún sứa is a coastal jellyfish noodle soup, especially familiar around Nha Trang and central beach towns. The broth is light; the jellyfish adds a crisp springy bite.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | jellyfish | light seafood broth | herbs | fish cake optional
good_to_know: Sứa means jellyfish. Order it when you are curious about a cool, crisp seafood texture that feels more like a beach-market salad than a heavy noodle bowl.
common_options: extra herbs | less chili | ask what seafood | no shrimp paste
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún sứa.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of jellyfish noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon soo-uh
what_it_is: Bún sứa is a light coastal noodle soup with jellyfish, herbs, and seafood broth. The jellyfish gives a crisp springy texture rather than a strong fish flavor.
how_to_enjoy: Eat the jellyfish with herbs and broth in the same bite. Add chili slowly so the light seafood flavor stays visible.
how_locals_order: Bún sứa is a texture order: cool, crisp jellyfish in a light seafood bowl. Ask what seafood is included and keep chili modest so you can still taste the delicate broth.
worth_knowing: Bún sứa is especially tied to central coastal cities such as Nha Trang. For travelers, the main surprise is the texture.
traveler_caution: Contains jellyfish and seafood broth.

at_a_glance: Hủ tiếu Nam Vang is a rice-noodle soup with clear savory broth, herbs, and pork and shrimp. It usually feels lighter and more flexible than richer beef soups.
usually_includes: broth | rice noodles | pork and shrimp | herbs | lime
good_to_know: If you want a milder bowl, ask for less spicy or no chili. The soup will still have plenty of flavor.
common_options: extra herbs | chili | bean sprouts | less spicy | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô hủ tiếu Nam Vang.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of Phnom Penh-style rice noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh hoo tee-ew nahm vahng
what_it_is: Hủ tiếu Nam Vang is a rice-noodle soup with a clear savory broth and toppings that often include pork, shrimp, herbs, and crisp vegetables. It can feel lighter and more flexible than heavier beef soups.
how_to_enjoy: Ask whether it comes nước or khô if the shop offers both: soup-style or dry with broth on the side. Add chili slowly because the clear broth is easy to overwhelm.
how_locals_order: With Hủ tiếu Nam Vang, locals may choose soup style or dry style. If you want the safer first bowl, order it as soup and add herbs, bean sprouts, lime, and chili little by little.
worth_knowing: The name points to Nam Vang, the Vietnamese name for Phnom Penh, and the dish is especially common in southern Vietnam. Treat that as menu context rather than one fixed recipe.
regional_association: southern Vietnam and Phnom Penh-style rice-noodle shops

at_a_glance: Hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho is a Mekong Delta rice-noodle soup from the Mỹ Tho style, known for clear broth, chewy noodles, pork, shrimp, herbs, and fried garlic.
usually_includes: rice noodles | pork or shrimp toppings | fried shallots | dry noodle dressing | clear side broth
good_to_know: Mỹ Tho is a Mekong Delta name to recognize. The dry version should still come with broth, because that clear, sweet side bowl is the backbone of the noodles.
common_options: soup style | dry style | extra herbs | no shrimp
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of mỹ Tho-style rice noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh hoo tee-ew mee taw
what_it_is: Hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho is a Mekong Delta rice-noodle soup with clear broth, chewy noodles, pork, shrimp, fried garlic, and herbs. It is lighter than phở but still satisfying.
how_to_enjoy: Ask whether the shop serves it nước or khô. For khô, mix the dry noodles with their savory dressing, then sip the clear pork-and-seafood broth from the side bowl between bites.
how_locals_order: Hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho is often worth ordering khô, dry style, if you want the toppings and fried garlic to stand out. Ask for soup on the side so you can alternate bites and broth.
worth_knowing: Mỹ Tho is a Mekong Delta city, and the name signals a southern rice-noodle style rather than a random topping.
regional_association: Mỹ Tho and the Mekong Delta
traveler_caution: Often contains pork and shrimp.

at_a_glance: Mì hoành thánh is wonton egg-noodle soup, usually with pork wontons, egg noodles, chives, and broth.
usually_includes: egg noodles | wontons | clear broth | greens | scallions
good_to_know: Ask for không cay if you want Mì hoành thánh without added chili.
common_options: less spicy | extra wontons | chili on the side | extra greens
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô mì hoành thánh.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of wonton egg noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee hwanh tanh
what_it_is: Mì hoành thánh is egg-noodle soup with wontons, a Vietnamese-Chinese shop classic. The bowl usually balances chewy yellow noodles, pork or shrimp wontons, greens, scallions, and a clear savory broth.
how_to_enjoy: Taste a wonton and a spoonful of broth before adding chili oil. The best bowls have springy noodles, tender wontons, and broth that stays clean enough to sip.
how_locals_order: Order mì hoành thánh when you want the wontons to be the point of the bowl. Ask for less chili or chili on the side if the shop adds chili oil by default.
worth_knowing: This is part of Vietnam’s Chinese-influenced noodle-shop language, especially visible in southern cities and older market neighborhoods.

at_a_glance: Mì gà is chicken egg-noodle soup, usually with springy mì, chicken, greens, and clear broth.
usually_includes: egg noodles | chicken | chicken broth | greens | scallions
good_to_know: Ask for không cay if you want Mì gà without added chili.
common_options: less spicy | extra greens | no chili | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô mì gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of chicken egg noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee gah
what_it_is: Mì gà is chicken egg-noodle soup: yellow noodles with chicken, greens, scallions, and a broth that should taste gently of poultry and aromatics.
how_to_enjoy: Lift the noodles while they are still springy, then sip the broth before adding chili. A little lime or herbs can brighten the chicken without hiding it.
how_locals_order: Order mì gà when you want chicken but prefer chewy egg noodles over rice noodles. Ask for less chili or extra greens before the bowl is finished.
worth_knowing: Mì signals wheat egg noodles on many Vietnamese menus, so mì gà reads differently from phở gà or miến gà even when the protein is the same.

at_a_glance: Miến gà is chicken glass-noodle soup, usually with slippery miến, shredded chicken, herbs, and clear broth.
usually_includes: glass noodles | chicken | chicken broth | scallions | pepper and herbs
good_to_know: Miến means glass noodles, so expect slippery transparent noodles in chicken broth, not wheat or egg noodles.
common_options: extra herbs | less spicy | no chili | no MSG
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô miến gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of chicken glass noodle soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee-en gah
what_it_is: Miến gà is chicken glass-noodle soup, lighter and silkier than egg-noodle bowls. The translucent noodles soak up chicken broth, pepper, scallions, and herbs.
how_to_enjoy: Eat the glass noodles before they soften too much, then season with pepper, lime, or chili only after tasting the broth. The clean chicken flavor should still come through.
how_locals_order: Order miến gà when you want a lighter chicken noodle bowl. Ask for extra herbs or no chili early, and use lime carefully so the broth stays delicate.
worth_knowing: Miến means glass noodles, a useful word for recognizing lighter soups and stir-fries across Vietnamese menus.

english_translation: Thick tapioca noodle soup with crab
at_a_glance: Bánh canh cua is thick tapioca-style noodle soup with crab, a glossy savory broth, herbs, and pepper. The noodles are chewy and spoonable, closer to udon texture than phở.
usually_includes: thick tapioca noodles | crab | savory broth | scallions | pepper
good_to_know: The broth can be slightly thick from the noodles. Ask about crab shell pieces if you want the easiest version to eat.
common_options: extra crab | quail egg | less pepper | ask about shells
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bánh canh cua.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of thick tapioca noodle soup with crab.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh bahn kan koo-ah
what_it_is: Bánh canh cua is crab soup with thick chewy noodles, glossy savory broth, scallions, pepper, and crab sweetness. The noodles are part of the comfort.
how_to_enjoy: Use a spoon and chopsticks together. Add pepper or chili after tasting because the crab broth can be delicate.
how_locals_order: Bánh canh cua comes with thick, chewy noodles and crab, so ask about shells before ordering. Extra crab or less pepper are useful tweaks, and the broth should feel savory rather than delicate.
worth_knowing: Bánh canh cua is loved in Vietnamese noodle shops for contrast: thick chewy noodles, crab sweetness, and a broth that can feel almost stew-like compared with clearer soups.
traveler_caution: Contains crab.

english_translation: Thick noodle soup with fish cakes
at_a_glance: Bánh canh chả cá is thick noodle soup with springy fish cakes and a light seafood broth. It is gentler than crab bánh canh but still has the chewy noodle texture.
usually_includes: thick tapioca noodles | fish cakes | seafood broth | scallions | pepper
good_to_know: Chả cá means fish cake here. The fish is usually formed into slices or patties, not a whole fillet.
common_options: extra fish cake | less pepper | extra herbs | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bánh canh chả cá.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of thick noodle soup with fish cakes.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh bahn kan chah kah
what_it_is: Bánh canh chả cá pairs thick chewy noodles with fish cakes and a light seafood broth. It is springy, gentle, and easier than many shellfish-heavy soups.
how_to_enjoy: Taste a fish cake with broth before adding lime or chili. The fish cake texture should be bouncy, not flaky.
how_locals_order: Bánh canh chả cá is the fish-cake version, so order it when you want springy fish cakes more than crab. Ask for extra chả cá or less pepper before the bowl is finished.
worth_knowing: Chả cá can mean fish cake in many everyday menu contexts, not only the famous Hanoi turmeric fish dish.

english_translation: Thick noodle soup with pork knuckle
at_a_glance: Bánh canh giò heo is thick noodle soup with pork knuckle, scallions, pepper, and a rich pork broth. It is heavier and more collagen-rich than the seafood versions.
usually_includes: thick tapioca noodles | pork knuckle | pork broth | scallions | pepper
good_to_know: Giò heo means pork knuckle. Expect bones and skin; ask for an easier cut if that is not what you want.
common_options: extra herbs | less pepper | ask for leaner pork | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bánh canh giò heo.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of thick noodle soup with pork knuckle.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh bahn kan yaw heh-oh
what_it_is: Bánh canh giò heo is thick noodle soup with pork knuckle, pork broth, scallions, and pepper. It is rich, chewy, and more rustic than a light chicken soup.
how_to_enjoy: Expect bones, skin, and tender pork. Ask for leaner pieces if you want less collagen and easier eating.
how_locals_order: Bánh canh giò heo is the pork-knuckle version, heavier and more collagen-rich than seafood bowls. Ask for leaner pieces or less pepper if you want the thick noodles without too much richness.
worth_knowing: Giò heo means pork knuckle, a texture Vietnamese diners often enjoy for richness and collagen; this bowl is about chew as much as broth.
traveler_caution: Contains pork knuckle with bones and skin.

at_a_glance: Cháo gà is chicken rice porridge, usually with shredded chicken, scallions, pepper, herbs, and sometimes fried dough sticks.
usually_includes: rice porridge | shredded chicken | ginger | scallions | black pepper
good_to_know: Cháo gà is gentle food, but not bland when it is good. Stir in pepper, herbs, or ginger gradually so the chicken broth stays soothing.
common_options: less pepper | extra chicken | no chili | fried dough sticks
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô cháo gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of chicken rice porridge.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh chow gah
what_it_is: Cháo gà is soft chicken rice porridge, comforting rather than flashy. It is often finished with shredded chicken, scallions, black pepper, herbs, and a little ginger or lime on the side.
how_to_enjoy: Stir gently, taste the porridge warm, then add pepper, lime, or herbs in small amounts. If quẩy is offered, dip the fried dough into the cháo for crunch.
how_locals_order: Order cháo gà when you want something gentle, warm, and easy to eat. Ask for less pepper or no chili if you want the chicken and rice comfort to stay mild.
worth_knowing: Cháo is Vietnam’s comfort-bowl language: breakfast, late-night food, sick-day food, and a soft landing when rich dishes feel like too much.

at_a_glance: Cháo lòng is pork offal rice porridge with ginger, herbs, pepper, and soft rice. It is warming and traditional, but more adventurous than chicken porridge.
usually_includes: rice porridge | pork offal | ginger | scallions | pepper
good_to_know: Lòng means offal or organs. If you want the gentle porridge experience without organs, choose cháo gà.
common_options: no offal | extra ginger | less pepper | with fried dough
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô cháo lòng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of pork offal rice porridge.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh chow lawng
what_it_is: Cháo lòng is rice porridge with pork offal, ginger, scallions, herbs, and pepper. It is soft and warming, but the toppings are more adventurous than chicken porridge.
how_to_enjoy: Add pepper, herbs, and ginger to brighten the bowl. Choose cháo gà if you want gentle porridge without offal.
how_locals_order: Cháo lòng is a comfort-bowl order, especially good when you want something soft. Ask for extra ginger or less pepper before mixing, and order fried dough on the side if the shop has it.
worth_knowing: Lòng means offal. This is a useful word to recognize if organ meats are a yes or no for you. In Vietnam, cháo is a rice-porridge comfort-food lane. The topping tells you whether the bowl stays gentle or turns more adventurous.
traveler_caution: Contains pork offal.

at_a_glance: Cháo hải sản is seafood rice porridge with soft rice, ginger, scallions, pepper, and whatever seafood the shop uses. It is gentle in texture but not always simple for allergies.
usually_includes: rice porridge | seafood | ginger | scallions | pepper
good_to_know: Hải sản means seafood. Ask what seafood is inside if shellfish matters.
common_options: extra ginger | less pepper | ask what seafood | with fried dough
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô cháo hải sản.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of seafood rice porridge.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh chow high sahn
what_it_is: Cháo hải sản is seafood congee: soft rice porridge with ginger, herbs, pepper, and seafood such as shrimp, squid, fish, or clams depending on the kitchen.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it hot and add pepper slowly. The ginger is there to keep the seafood flavor clean.
how_locals_order: Cháo hải sản is a comfort-bowl order, especially good when you want something soft. Ask for extra ginger or less pepper before mixing, and order fried dough on the side if the shop has it.
worth_knowing: Cháo is comfort food, but hải sản turns it into a seafood order. That word matters for shellfish allergies. In Vietnam, cháo is a rice-porridge comfort-food lane. The topping tells you whether the bowl stays gentle or turns more adventurous.
traveler_caution: Contains seafood and may include shellfish.

at_a_glance: Bún chả pairs smoky grilled pork with rice vermicelli, herbs, and a warm nước chấm dipping broth. The charm is sweet-savory pork, cool noodles, and bright herbs in the same bite.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | grilled pork | fresh herbs | nước chấm | pickled vegetables
good_to_know: Nước chấm here is a warm fish-sauce dipping broth with sweetness, vinegar or lime, garlic, and chili.
common_options: extra herbs | extra nước chấm | no chili | add fried rolls
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bún chả.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of grilled pork with vermicelli.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn boon chah
what_it_is: Bún chả is grilled pork served with rice vermicelli, herbs, pickles, and warm nước chấm dipping broth. It should smell smoky, taste sweet-savory, and feel fresh from the herbs.
how_to_enjoy: Dip noodles and herbs into the warm nước chấm bowl with the grilled pork, or build small bites with noodle, herb, and pork together. The broth-like fish-sauce dip is the center of the dish.
how_locals_order: Order bún chả as a set: grilled pork in warm nước chấm, noodles, herbs, and often fried rolls if available. Ask for no chili in the nước chấm before it reaches the table.
worth_knowing: This Hanoi staple is not just grilled pork plus noodles; the warm sweet-sour fish-sauce bowl is what ties the smoke, herbs, and cool bún together.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Bún thịt nướng is rice vermicelli with lemongrass grilled pork, usually with herbs, pickles, peanuts, scallion oil, and nước chấm.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | grilled pork | fresh herbs | nước chấm | peanuts
good_to_know: Nước chấm is the dressing here; it is meant to season the noodles, not sit untouched on the side.
common_options: nước chấm on the side | more herbs | no chili | no peanuts
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bún thịt nướng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of grilled pork vermicelli bowl.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn boon tit noong
what_it_is: Bún thịt nướng is a cool rice-vermicelli bowl with lemongrass grilled pork, herbs, pickles, peanuts, scallion oil, and nước chấm for tossing through the noodles.
how_to_enjoy: Pour the nước chấm over the vermicelli little by little, then toss from the bottom so grilled pork, herbs, pickles, peanuts, and noodles mix evenly.
how_locals_order: Order bún thịt nướng when you want a cool noodle bowl with smoky pork. Ask for nước chấm on the side or no chili if you want to control the sweet-sour fish-sauce dressing.
worth_knowing: This southern-style bowl is about contrast: warm grilled pork, cool bún, crunchy pickles, herbs, peanuts, and a bright pour of nước chấm.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Bún nem nướng is rice vermicelli with grilled pork sausage, usually with herbs, peanuts, pickles, and a thick Nha Trang-style peanut-garlic dip.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | grilled pork sausage | fresh herbs | thick Nha Trang-style peanut-garlic dip | crispy crunch
good_to_know: May contain pork.
common_options: sauce on the side | more herbs | no chili | no peanuts
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bún nem nướng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of grilled pork sausage vermicelli bowl.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn boon nem noong
what_it_is: Bún nem nướng is the Vietnamese name to look for when you want rice vermicelli with grilled pork sausage. The supporting pieces, often herbs, peanuts, pickles, and a thick Nha Trang-style peanut-garlic dip, are not extras; they complete the bite.
how_to_enjoy: Toss the grilled pork sausage, herbs, pickles, peanuts, and vermicelli with the thick peanut-garlic dip a little at a time. The dip is rich, so pacing it keeps the bowl bright.
how_locals_order: Order bún nem nướng for the bouncy grilled pork sausage and thick Nha Trang-style dip. Say no peanuts or no chili before mixing if either matters.
worth_knowing: Nem nướng is especially tied to south-central food culture; in a bún bowl it turns into a cool, crunchy, smoky meal rather than a soup.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Bún bò Nam Bộ is southern beef noodle salad, usually with warm beef, herbs, peanuts, fried shallots, and sweet-tart fish sauce.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | seared beef | fresh herbs | nước chấm | peanuts or fried shallots
good_to_know: The fish-sauce dressing goes over the bowl and gets tossed through the noodles, herbs, beef, peanuts, and fried shallots. Pour gradually if you want more control over sweetness and salt.
common_options: nước chấm on the side | no peanuts | extra herbs | less spicy
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bún bò Nam Bộ.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of southern beef vermicelli salad.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn boon baw nahm boh
what_it_is: Bún bò Nam Bộ is a southern dry noodle bowl with warm beef, herbs, peanuts, fried shallots, and sweet-tart fish-sauce dressing. It tastes best once everything is mixed through the noodles.
how_to_enjoy: Toss the warm stir-fried beef through the cool vermicelli with herbs, bean sprouts, peanuts, fried shallots, and fish-sauce dressing. The bowl should taste smoky, nutty, fresh, and tangy at once.
how_locals_order: Order bún bò Nam Bộ when you want beef without broth. Ask for no peanuts or nước chấm on the side before the bowl is tossed.
worth_knowing: Despite the name, this is not bún bò Huế. It is a dry southern-style beef vermicelli bowl where texture and dressing do the work.

at_a_glance: Bún bò xào is stir-fried beef over cool rice vermicelli with herbs, pickles, peanuts or fried shallots, and nước chấm. It is savory, bright, and built for mixing.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | stir-fried beef | fresh herbs | nước chấm | peanuts or fried shallots
good_to_know: Nước chấm is the usual sauce: fish sauce balanced with lime, sugar, garlic, and chili. Start with half, mix, then add more if the noodles need it.
common_options: extra nước chấm | more herbs | no chili | no peanuts
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bún bò xào.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of stir-fried beef over vermicelli.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn boon baw sow
what_it_is: Bún bò xào is stir-fried beef over cool rice vermicelli with herbs, pickles, peanuts or fried shallots, and nước chấm. It is savory, bright, crunchy, and built for mixing.
how_to_enjoy: Pour the nước chấm gradually, then mix so the beef juices, herbs, noodles, and crunch share the flavor. Ask for no chili or no peanuts before it is assembled.
how_locals_order: Bún bò xào eats more like a beef noodle salad than a soup. Ask for no peanuts or extra herbs before mixing, then add nước chấm in small pours so the beef stays bright.
worth_knowing: Nước chấm is the usual sauce: fish sauce balanced with lime, sugar, garlic, and chili. It is a dressing for the bowl, not a thick gravy. In Vietnamese dry noodle and vermicelli bowls, cool herbs, warm toppings, sauce, crunch, and soft noodles all matter.

at_a_glance: Bún gà nướng is rice vermicelli with grilled chicken, usually with herbs, cucumber, pickles, peanuts, and nước chấm.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | grilled chicken | fresh herbs | nước chấm | fried shallots
good_to_know: Ask for nước mắm riêng if you want to control the sweet-salty fish-sauce dressing over the noodles.
common_options: nước chấm on the side | no peanuts | extra herbs | less spicy
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bún gà nướng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of grilled chicken vermicelli bowl.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn boon gah noong
what_it_is: Bún gà nướng is grilled chicken over cool rice vermicelli with herbs, pickles, peanuts, and nước chấm. It is lighter than a rice plate but still smoky and filling.
how_to_enjoy: Pour nước chấm slowly, then toss the grilled chicken, herbs, pickles, peanuts, and bún from the bottom. The smoky chicken should meet the cool noodles in every bite.
how_locals_order: Order bún gà nướng when you want the grilled flavor of a chicken plate but in a fresh noodle bowl. Ask for no peanuts or no chili before the bowl is assembled.
worth_knowing: This is a good first dry-bún order for travelers: familiar grilled chicken, but with the herb-and-nước-chấm rhythm that makes Vietnamese noodle bowls sing.

at_a_glance: Bún chả cá is rice vermicelli with springy fish cakes, herbs, fried shallots, and a light sauce or broth depending on the shop. It should taste seafood-savory, fresh, and gentle.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | fish cakes | fresh herbs | nước chấm or light broth | fried shallots
good_to_know: Contains fish; ask about bones if the shop also adds fish pieces.
common_options: extra fish cakes | more herbs | less chili | extra noodles
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bún chả cá.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of vermicelli noodles with fish cakes.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn boon chah kah
what_it_is: Bún chả cá is rice vermicelli with springy fish cakes, herbs, fried shallots, and a light sauce or broth depending on the shop. The flavor is seafood-savory and gentler than pork-heavy vermicelli bowls.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the fish cakes first, then add herbs, chili, or lime-pepper salt dip or ginger fish sauce gradually. If it comes with broth, sip before adding lime or chili.
how_locals_order: Bún chả cá is about fish cakes, not pork. Ask whether the shop serves it as a broth bowl or a drier noodle plate, then add herbs, lime, and chili after tasting the fish broth or fish-cake seasoning.
worth_knowing: Chả cá means fish cake here, a springy seafood topping common in central coastal noodle shops.

english_translation: Vermicelli with tofu and shrimp paste
at_a_glance: Bún đậu mắm tôm is a northern-style platter of rice vermicelli, fried tofu, herbs, and pungent shrimp-paste sauce. It is salty, vivid, and defined by the mắm tôm, a pungent fermented shrimp-paste dip.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | fried tofu | fresh herbs | mắm tôm | pork optional
good_to_know: Mắm tôm is fermented shrimp-paste sauce with a strong aroma. Many places can offer a milder nước chấm dip if you ask.
common_options: mắm tôm on the side | milder nước chấm | more herbs | no pork
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bún đậu mắm tôm.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of vermicelli with tofu and shrimp paste.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn boon dow mahm tom
what_it_is: Bún đậu mắm tôm is a platter of rice vermicelli, fried tofu, herbs, and pungent shrimp-paste sauce, often with pork or other add-ons. It is vivid, salty, and very different from a tidy noodle bowl.
how_to_enjoy: Try the mắm tôm carefully first; mắm tôm is strong even for confident eaters. If the aroma feels like too much, ask whether a milder fish-sauce dip is available.
how_locals_order: Bún đậu mắm tôm is all about the mắm tôm shrimp-paste dip, so ask for it riêng if you want control. If the smell feels too intense, ask for nước chấm instead and keep the herbs generous.
worth_knowing: Bún đậu mắm tôm is closely tied to casual northern Vietnam snacking and sharing. Mắm tôm is the defining choice here: pungent fermented shrimp paste with tofu, herbs, noodles, and shared bites.
traveler_caution: Contains shrimp paste and may include pork.

english_translation: Duck and bamboo shoot vermicelli soup
at_a_glance: Bún măng vịt is duck and bamboo-shoot vermicelli soup, usually served with herbs and a ginger fish-sauce dip for the duck.
usually_includes: rice vermicelli | duck | bamboo shoots | herbs | ginger fish-sauce dip
good_to_know: Duck often comes with a ginger fish-sauce dip on the side. Use it for the meat, then taste the broth before adding extra chili.
common_options: extra herbs | less spicy | ginger fish sauce on the side | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô bún măng vịt.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of duck and bamboo shoot vermicelli soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh boon mahng veet
what_it_is: Bún măng vịt pairs duck broth, rice vermicelli, bamboo shoots, herbs, and duck meat often dipped in ginger fish sauce. The bamboo keeps the broth earthy and clean.
how_to_enjoy: Taste the broth, then alternate noodles with bites of duck dipped lightly in ginger fish sauce. Add herbs and chili slowly so the duck flavor stays clear.
how_locals_order: Order bún măng vịt when you want duck soup with a separate ginger fish-sauce bite. Ask for less chili in the dip if you want the bamboo broth and duck to lead.
worth_knowing: Duck noodle soups often depend on the side dip as much as the broth. Ginger, fish sauce, and chili cut through the richness of the duck. In Vietnam, bún măng vịt sits closer to a soup meal than a dry noodle bowl; the duck, bamboo-shoot broth, herbs, and ginger dip make it read local.

at_a_glance: Cao lầu is a Hội An noodle bowl with chewy noodles, pork, herbs, crisp bits, and a small amount of seasoned pork sauce. It is more concentrated and local-specialty than soup-like.
usually_includes: chewy rice noodles | pork | fresh herbs | savory pork sauce | crispy rice crackers
good_to_know: Cao lầu is not a soup bowl and not a dip bowl. The shallow pork coating should cling to the thick Hội An noodles while herbs, bean sprouts, and cracklings keep each bite lively.
common_options: extra herbs | no chili | extra rice crackers | less pork sauce
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cao lầu.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of Hội An pork noodle dish.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn cow low
what_it_is: Cao lầu is Hội An’s famous dry noodle bowl: chewy noodles, slices of pork, herbs, crisp rice crackers, and a shallow savory pork sauce that coats rather than floods the bowl.
how_to_enjoy: Break the rice crackers over the noodles, then toss everything so the pork sauce clings to the cao lầu noodles. It should eat like a sauced noodle bowl, not soup.
how_locals_order: Order cao lầu in Hội An when you want the local noodle texture. Ask for extra herbs or no chili, but keep the shallow pork sauce; it is part of what makes the dish cao lầu.
worth_knowing: Cao lầu is strongly associated with Hội An, and travelers often remember it for the chewy noodles and herb pile as much as the pork.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Mì Quảng gà is a Quảng Nam-style chicken noodle bowl with wide turmeric rice noodles, shallow chicken broth, herbs, peanuts, and a crisp rice cracker. It is a central-Vietnam dish, not a soup.
usually_includes: wide turmeric rice noodles | chicken | turmeric broth | peanuts | rice cracker
good_to_know: The broth is intentionally shallow and concentrated. Mix before adding lime or chili so the turmeric broth coats the noodles.
common_options: extra herbs | less chili | extra broth | no peanuts
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô mì Quảng gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of quảng-style turmeric noodles with chicken.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee kwahng gah
what_it_is: Mì Quảng gà is a central-Vietnam noodle bowl with wide turmeric rice noodles, chicken, herbs, peanuts, rice cracker, and shallow broth. It should look half-dry compared with soup.
how_to_enjoy: Break some rice cracker into the bowl, mix the shallow broth through the noodles, then add lime or chili. Do not expect the broth to cover everything.
how_locals_order: Mì Quảng gà should arrive with turmeric rice noodles, peanuts, herbs, and only a shallow amount of broth. Ask for extra broth if you prefer it wetter, and say no peanuts before the bowl is built.
worth_knowing: Mì Quảng is associated with Quảng Nam and central Vietnam. Its shallow broth, turmeric noodles, herbs, peanuts, and rice cracker are the signature.
traveler_caution: Often contains peanuts.

english_translation: Quảng-style turmeric noodles with shrimp and pork
at_a_glance: Mì Quảng tôm thịt is the shrimp-and-pork version of Quảng-style turmeric noodles, with herbs, peanuts, rice cracker, and just enough broth to stain the noodles golden.
usually_includes: wide turmeric rice noodles | shrimp and pork | turmeric broth | peanuts | rice cracker
good_to_know: This commonly includes both shellfish and pork. Ask before ordering if either one matters.
common_options: less spicy | no peanuts | extra rice cracker | extra herbs
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô mì Quảng tôm thịt.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of quảng-style turmeric noodles with shrimp and pork.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee kwahng tom tit
what_it_is: Mì Quảng tôm thịt is a central Vietnamese turmeric-noodle bowl with shrimp, pork, herbs, peanuts, rice crackers, and a shallow yellow broth. The broth seasons the noodles instead of filling the bowl.
how_to_enjoy: Crack the rice cracker into the bowl, mix the herbs and peanuts through, and let the shallow turmeric broth coat the noodles. Add lime or chili after tasting the broth.
how_locals_order: Order mì Quảng tôm thịt when you want the classic shrimp-and-pork version. Ask for less chili or no peanuts before mixing, but expect only a small amount of broth.
worth_knowing: Mì Quảng is a signature of Quảng Nam and Đà Nẵng food culture; the “almost dry” broth level is intentional.
traveler_caution: Contains shrimp, pork, and often peanuts.

at_a_glance: Mì xào bò is stir-fried egg noodles with beef, usually with greens, garlic, onion, and glossy sauce.
usually_includes: egg noodles | beef | fresh herbs | garlic-fish-sauce stir-fry glaze | fried shallots or crunchy topping
good_to_know: Ask for không cay if you want Mì xào bò without added chili.
common_options: less spicy | less oil | extra vegetables | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô mì xào bò.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of stir-fried egg noodles with beef.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee sow baw
what_it_is: Mì xào bò is wok-fried egg noodles with beef, vegetables, garlic, and a glossy savory seasoning. The appeal is hot-wok aroma and chewy noodles, not broth.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it while the noodles are still springy and the beef is hot from the wok. Add chili or soy-lime seasoning lightly so the garlic and beef stay clear.
how_locals_order: Order mì xào bò when you want stir-fried noodles. Ask ít dầu for less oil, ít cay for less chili, or thêm rau if you want more greens.
worth_knowing: Xào means stir-fried, a key menu word for recognizing fast wok dishes across Vietnam.

at_a_glance: Mì xào hải sản is stir-fried noodles with seafood, usually with shrimp, squid, greens, garlic, and fish-sauce-and-garlic glaze.
usually_includes: egg noodles | seafood | fresh herbs | garlic-fish-sauce stir-fry glaze | fried shallots or crunchy topping
good_to_know: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
common_options: less spicy | less oil | extra vegetables | ask about shellfish
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô mì xào hải sản.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of stir-fried egg noodles with seafood.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee sow high sahn
what_it_is: Mì xào hải sản is wok-fried egg noodles with seafood such as shrimp, squid, or fish cake, plus vegetables and garlic. It should taste briny, hot, and a little smoky from the pan.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it soon after it lands so the noodles keep their chew and the seafood stays tender. Ask about shellfish before ordering if allergies matter.
how_locals_order: Order mì xào hải sản for a seafood noodle plate rather than soup. Ask ít cay, ít dầu, or không hải sản có vỏ if you need less chili, less oil, or no shellfish.
worth_knowing: At casual shops, hải sản can mean a mix of shrimp, squid, fish cake, or whatever seafood the kitchen has ready.
traveler_caution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.

at_a_glance: Mì khô is dry egg noodles, usually with char siu or chicken, greens, sauce, and a side bowl of broth.
usually_includes: egg noodles | savory toppings | fried shallots | greens | side broth
good_to_know: Khô means dry, but a small broth bowl often comes with it; that two-part eating style is normal.
common_options: side broth | extra fried shallots | extra greens | less spicy
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô mì khô.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of dry egg noodles.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee koh
what_it_is: Mì khô is dry egg noodles mixed with savory seasoning, char siu, chicken, or other toppings, fried shallots, greens, and often a clear broth served on the side.
how_to_enjoy: Mix from the bottom so the seasoning coats the noodles, then sip the side broth between bites. Add chili slowly so the shallot crunch and noodle chew stay clear.
how_locals_order: Order mì khô when you want noodles without soup. Ask for broth on the side, extra fried shallots, or less chili before the bowl is mixed.
worth_knowing: Mì khô belongs to Vietnam's dry-noodle rhythm, where mixing at the table is part of the meal rather than a final flourish.

at_a_glance: Hủ tiếu khô is dry hủ tiếu noodles, usually with minced pork, shrimp or slices, herbs, sauce, and broth on the side.
usually_includes: rice noodles | pork or shrimp toppings | fried shallots | savory dry noodle dressing | clear side broth
good_to_know: Khô means dry-style, but the broth still matters. Many southern shops serve it on the side so you get both chewy dressed noodles and a clean pork-seafood broth.
common_options: side broth | less spicy | extra herbs | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô hủ tiếu khô.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of dry rice noodles.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh hoo tee-ew koh
what_it_is: Hủ tiếu khô is the dry version of southern hủ tiếu: noodles tossed with savory seasoning, toppings, herbs, and often a separate clear broth on the side.
how_to_enjoy: Mix the noodles first so the dressing coats them, then sip the side broth between bites. Add lime, chili, and greens slowly so the dry bowl keeps its balance.
how_locals_order: Order hủ tiếu khô when you want the noodle flavor concentrated instead of in soup. Ask for soup on the side if it is not obvious, and say less chili before mixing.
worth_knowing: Khô means dry, but the order often still includes broth separately; that two-part rhythm is the point.

at_a_glance: Miến xào cua is glass noodles stir-fried with crab, usually with sweet crab meat, egg, onion, herbs, and pepper.
usually_includes: glass noodles | crab | garlic | garlic-fish-sauce stir-fry glaze | herbs
good_to_know: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
common_options: less spicy | less oil | share size | ask about shell
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô miến xào cua.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of stir-fried glass noodles with crab.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee-en sow koo-ah
what_it_is: Miến xào cua is glass noodles wok-tossed with crab, garlic, scallions, and the sweet juices from the crab. The noodles turn glossy as they soak up the seafood flavor.
how_to_enjoy: Share it while hot, lifting the glass noodles gently so the crab stays distributed. Ask before ordering if you want to avoid shell pieces.
how_locals_order: Order miến xào cua as a shared crab noodle plate. Ask for less oil or less chili before the wok fires, and check whether the crab comes in shell.
worth_knowing: This is a celebratory seafood-noodle order in many Vietnamese restaurants because crab perfumes the whole plate.
traveler_caution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.

at_a_glance: Miến xào hải sản is glass noodles stir-fried with seafood, usually with shrimp, squid, vegetables, and garlic.
usually_includes: glass noodles | seafood | garlic | garlic-fish-sauce stir-fry glaze | herbs
good_to_know: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
common_options: less spicy | less oil | ask about shellfish | extra vegetables
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô miến xào hải sản.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of stir-fried glass noodles with seafood.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh mee-en sow high sahn
what_it_is: Miến xào hải sản is glass noodles stir-fried with shrimp, squid, fish cake, or mixed seafood. The noodles soak up garlic, seafood juices, and wok seasoning.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it hot while the glass noodles are slippery and the seafood is tender. If shellfish is a concern, ask what seafood is included before ordering.
how_locals_order: Order miến xào hải sản for a shared seafood noodle plate. Ask ít cay, ít dầu, or no shellfish before the wok starts.
worth_knowing: In Vietnam, miến turns translucent and springy, so this seafood plate feels lighter than egg-noodle stir-fries even when the shrimp and squid flavor is strong.
traveler_caution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.

english_translation: Fine rice vermicelli sheets with grilled pork
at_a_glance: Bánh hỏi thịt nướng is fine rice-noodle sheets with grilled pork, usually with scallion oil, herbs, rice paper, and nước chấm.
usually_includes: fine rice vermicelli sheets | grilled pork | scallion oil | fresh herbs | rice paper and nước chấm
good_to_know: May contain pork.
common_options: extra rice paper | extra herbs | no chili | extra nước chấm
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh hỏi thịt nướng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of fine rice vermicelli sheets with grilled pork.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn hoy tit noong
what_it_is: Bánh hỏi thịt nướng pairs delicate woven rice-noodle sheets with grilled pork, scallion oil, herbs, rice paper, and nước chấm. It is often eaten as small wrapped bites.
how_to_enjoy: Use rice paper if it is served: layer bánh hỏi, grilled pork, herbs, and cucumber, then dip lightly in nước chấm. The noodle sheets are delicate, so do not drown them.
how_locals_order: Order bánh hỏi thịt nướng when you want a roll-your-own grilled pork plate. Ask for extra rice paper, extra herbs, or no chili in the nước chấm before everyone starts wrapping.
worth_knowing: In Vietnam, bánh hỏi makes grilled pork feel elegant: tiny noodle sheets carry scallion oil, smoke, herbs, and fish-sauce brightness in one bite.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

english_translation: Fine rice vermicelli sheets with roasted pork
at_a_glance: Bánh hỏi heo quay is fine woven rice noodles with roast pork, usually with crackling heo quay, scallion oil, herbs, and fish sauce.
usually_includes: fine rice vermicelli sheets | roasted pork | scallion oil | fresh herbs | rice paper and nước chấm
good_to_know: May contain pork.
common_options: extra rice paper | extra herbs | no chili | extra nước chấm
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh hỏi heo quay.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of fine rice vermicelli sheets with roasted pork.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn hoy heh-oh kway
what_it_is: Bánh hỏi heo quay pairs fine woven rice-noodle sheets with roast pork and crackling, scallion oil, herbs, and nước chấm. The joy is delicate noodles against crisp pork skin.
how_to_enjoy: Build small bites with bánh hỏi, roast pork, herbs, and rice paper if served, then dip lightly in nước chấm. Keep the crackling dry enough to stay crisp.
how_locals_order: Order bánh hỏi heo quay for a shareable plate of crackling pork and fine noodle sheets. Ask for extra rice paper or herbs if you want to eat it the local wrap-and-dip way.
worth_knowing: This is the richer cousin of grilled-pork bánh hỏi, often chosen for parties or family tables because the pork skin brings crunch.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

english_translation: Broken rice with grilled pork chop
at_a_glance: Cơm tấm sườn is a classic southern broken-rice plate with grilled pork chop, scallion oil, pickles, cucumber, and a sweet-savory nước mắm dressing.
usually_includes: broken rice | grilled pork chop | scallion oil | pickles and cucumber | nước mắm dressing
good_to_know: The small bowl is usually sweet-savory nước mắm dressing. Pour it over the rice and pork a little at a time so the grains stay glossy, not flooded.
common_options: nước mắm on the side | add fried egg | extra pickles | less spicy
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm tấm sườn.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of broken rice with grilled pork chop.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum tahm swoon
what_it_is: Cơm tấm sườn is a broken-rice plate with grilled pork chop, pickles, scallion oil, and fish-sauce dressing. It is smoky, savory, and built like a complete meal.
how_to_enjoy: Spoon nước mắm over the broken rice gradually, then cut the grilled pork into bites with pickles and scallion oil. The fish-sauce dressing should brighten the plate without soaking it.
how_locals_order: Order cơm tấm sườn for the classic grilled pork broken-rice plate. Ask for nước mắm riêng if you want the fish-sauce dressing on the side, or thêm trứng if you want an egg.
worth_knowing: Cơm tấm grew from broken rice grains that were once humble, practical food in southern Vietnam and Saigon. Today it is a beloved everyday plate because smoky pork, scallion oil, and nước mắm turn those grains into comfort food.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

english_translation: Broken rice with pork chop, shredded pork, and egg meatloaf
at_a_glance: Cơm tấm bì chả sườn is a loaded broken-rice plate: grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, steamed egg meatloaf, pickles, scallion oil, and fish-sauce dressing.
usually_includes: broken rice | grilled pork chop | shredded pork skin | egg meatloaf | fish-sauce dressing
good_to_know: Bì is shredded pork skin with toasted rice powder; chả is the steamed egg-and-pork loaf.
common_options: nước mắm on the side | extra pickles | add fried egg | less spicy
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm tấm bì chả sườn.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of broken rice with pork chop, shredded pork, and egg meatloaf.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum tahm bee chah swoon
what_it_is: Cơm tấm bì chả sườn is a southern broken-rice plate with grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, egg meatloaf, pickles, scallion oil, and fish-sauce dressing.
how_to_enjoy: Use the nước mắm to season the broken rice, then rotate bites of grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, steamed egg loaf, pickles, and scallion oil.
how_locals_order: Order cơm tấm bì chả sườn when you want the full texture set without the fried-egg add-on. Ask for nước mắm riêng or extra pickles before the plate is dressed.
worth_knowing: Cơm tấm began with broken rice grains from milling, associated with southern Vietnam and Saigon working-day eating. Bì, chả, and sườn show how a humble rice base became a beloved loaded plate.
traveler_caution: Contains pork, egg, and fish sauce.

vietnamese_item: Cơm tấm sườn bì chả trứng
english_translation: Broken rice with pork chop, shredded pork, meatloaf, and egg
romanized_no_tones: Com tam suon bi cha trung
sound_out: kum tahm swoon bee chah choong
at_a_glance: Cơm tấm sườn bì chả trứng is the maximal broken-rice plate: pork chop, shredded pork skin, egg meatloaf, fried egg, pickles, scallion oil, and nước mắm.
usually_includes: broken rice | grilled pork chop | shredded pork skin | egg meatloaf | fried egg
good_to_know: This is one of the most complete cơm tấm orders; it can be a big meal.
common_options: nước mắm on the side | extra pickles | less spicy | extra rice
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm tấm sườn bì chả trứng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of broken rice with pork chop, shredded pork, meatloaf, and egg.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum tahm swoon bee chah choong
what_it_is: Cơm tấm sườn bì chả trứng is a full broken-rice combo with grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, egg meatloaf, fried egg, pickles, scallion oil, and nước mắm.
how_to_enjoy: Treat it as a loaded broken-rice plate: pork chop for smoke, bì for nutty chew, chả for softness, egg for richness, and nước mắm to tie the rice together.
how_locals_order: Order cơm tấm sườn bì chả trứng when you want the works. Ask for nước mắm riêng if you want to control sweetness, salt, and chili on the rice.
worth_knowing: This is the loaded cơm tấm order, built from southern Vietnam’s broken-rice tradition: grilled pork for smoke, bì for chew, chả for eggy softness, and trứng for extra richness.
traveler_caution: Contains pork, egg, and fish sauce.

at_a_glance: Cơm sườn nướng is rice with a grilled pork chop, pickles, cucumber, scallion oil, and nước mắm. It is the straightforward cousin of cơm tấm.
usually_includes: rice | grilled pork chop | pickles | scallion oil | fish-sauce dressing
good_to_know: Sườn here usually means pork chop or cutlet, not American barbecue ribs.
common_options: nước mắm on the side | extra pickles | add fried egg | less spicy
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm sườn nướng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of rice with grilled pork chop.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum swoon noong
what_it_is: Cơm sườn nướng is grilled pork over rice, usually with pickles, cucumber, scallion oil, and nước mắm. It is the simpler rice-plate cousin of cơm tấm sườn.
how_to_enjoy: Cut the pork into the rice, add pickles for crunch, then spoon nước mắm gradually. The scallion oil and grilled edges should stay noticeable.
how_locals_order: Order cơm sườn nướng when you want a straightforward grilled pork rice plate. Ask for nước mắm riêng, extra pickles, or less chili before the plate is finished.
worth_knowing: Rice plates are everyday lunch language in Vietnam: fast, filling, and anchored by one strong protein plus pickles and nước mắm.
traveler_caution: Contains pork and fish sauce.

at_a_glance: Cơm gà Hội An is Hội An chicken rice: turmeric-tinted rice, shredded or chopped chicken, herbs, onion, chili-lime seasoning, and often a small side broth.
usually_includes: turmeric rice | chicken | herbs | onion | chili-lime seasoning
good_to_know: This is not plain chicken on rice. The rice, herbs, and chili-lime onion mixture are what make it taste like Hội An.
common_options: less chili | extra herbs | side broth | extra chicken
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm gà Hội An.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of Hội An chicken rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum gah hoy ahn
what_it_is: Cơm gà Hội An is Hội An chicken rice with turmeric-tinted rice, chicken, herbs, onion, and a bright chili-lime seasoning. The rice is as important as the chicken.
how_to_enjoy: Mix some herbs and onion through the rice, then add chili-lime seasoning carefully. Ask for less chili if you want the chicken and rice to stay gentle.
how_locals_order: Cơm gà Hội An is a Hội An-style chicken rice order, so ask for less chili if the shredded chicken salad looks fiery. Extra herbs and side broth are good local-feeling additions.
worth_knowing: The Hội An name matters because the rice, shredded chicken, herbs, and chili-lime onion mixture belong to the old-town chicken-rice style. It should taste brighter and more fragrant than plain chicken over rice.

at_a_glance: Cơm gà xối mỡ is crispy fried chicken over rice, often with chicken-fat fragrance, pickles, cucumber, and a muối tiêu chanh, a lime-pepper salt dip. It is about crisp skin against hot rice.
usually_includes: rice | crispy fried chicken | pickles | cucumber | muối tiêu chanh, a lime-pepper salt dip
good_to_know: Xối mỡ points to hot fat/oil poured over the chicken for crispness. It is not a sticky-rice dish.
common_options: extra pickles | lime-pepper salt on the side | less oil | extra rice
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm gà xối mỡ.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of fried chicken rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum gah soy muh
what_it_is: Cơm gà xối mỡ is fried or oil-crisped chicken over rice, often with pickles, cucumber, scallion oil, and a light broth or lime-pepper salt on the side.
how_to_enjoy: Eat the chicken skin while it is still crisp, then use pickles and cucumber to cut the richness. Lime-pepper salt is for small dips, not for covering the rice.
how_locals_order: Order cơm gà xối mỡ when you want crispy chicken with rice. Ask for extra pickles, less oil, or lime-pepper salt on the side if you want more control.
worth_knowing: Cơm gà xối mỡ is a useful bridge dish for travelers: fried chicken and rice feel familiar, while the chicken-fat aroma, pickles, and lime-pepper salt make it distinctly Vietnamese.

at_a_glance: Vietnam’s take on Hainanese chicken rice: silky poached chicken, fragrant rice, cucumber, herbs, side broth, and ginger-scallion, chili, or soy dips.
usually_includes: fragrant chicken rice | poached chicken | cucumber | side broth | ginger-scallion or chili dip
good_to_know: It is usually mild and a strong option when you want a filling but not spicy meal.
common_options: extra ginger-scallion dip | side broth | extra rice | less chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm gà Hải Nam.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of Hainanese-style chicken rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum gah high nahm
what_it_is: Cơm gà Hải Nam serves poached chicken over rice cooked with chicken fat or broth, often with cucumber, pickles, soup, and ginger-scallion, chili, or soy-based dips.
how_to_enjoy: Try the chicken with each dip before mixing everything. The rice is not a background starch here; it should taste gently of chicken and aromatics.
how_locals_order: Order cơm gà Hải Nam when you want fragrant rice and gentle chicken rather than heavy spice. Ask for extra ginger-scallion dip or side broth for the full chicken-rice rhythm.
worth_knowing: The dish reflects the Chinese diaspora's influence in Vietnamese cities, adapted into everyday rice-shop language with Vietnamese herbs, pickles, and dipping habits.

at_a_glance: Cơm bò lúc lắc is rice with shaking beef, usually with seared beef cubes, tomato, greens, onion, and lime-pepper salt.
usually_includes: rice | shaking beef cubes | onion and bell pepper | lime-pepper salt | pickles or salad
good_to_know: Lime-pepper salt is for the beef cubes, while the rice catches the wok juices. Ask for onion or pepper changes before the beef hits the pan.
common_options: lime-pepper salt on the side | less onion | extra rice | less spicy
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm bò lúc lắc.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of shaking beef with rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum baw look lak
what_it_is: Cơm bò lúc lắc is rice topped with seared beef cubes, onion or bell pepper, lettuce, tomato, and a lime-pepper salt dip. The beef should taste hot from the wok and slightly caramelized.
how_to_enjoy: Dip the beef cubes lightly in lime-pepper salt, then eat with rice, tomato, and greens. Too much dip can hide the seared beef flavor.
how_locals_order: Order cơm bò lúc lắc when you want shaking beef as a rice plate. Ask for less pepper, less onion, or lime-pepper salt on the side before the wok order lands.
worth_knowing: Lúc lắc refers to the shaking motion of the beef in the wok, a useful phrase to recognize on Vietnamese menus.

english_translation: Rice with stir-fried beef and onions
at_a_glance: Cơm bò xào hành tây is rice with beef stir-fried with onions, garlic, and wok seasoning. It is a hot-wok comfort plate, not a stew.
usually_includes: rice | stir-fried beef | onion | garlic | savory garlic-fish-sauce stir-fry glaze
good_to_know: Hành tây means onion. Order this when you want beef-and-rice with a familiar sautéed-onion flavor.
common_options: fried egg | extra rice | less garlic-fish-sauce stir-fry glaze | extra pickles
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm bò xào hành tây.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of rice with stir-fried beef and onions.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum baw sow hanh tay
what_it_is: Cơm bò xào hành tây is a beef-and-onion stir-fry served over rice.
how_to_enjoy: Let the garlic-fish-sauce stir-fry glaze season the rice. Ask for less onion only before the dish is cooked.
how_locals_order: For Cơm bò xào hành tây, name the plate and then choose the practical add-on: fried egg or extra rice. Locals balance rice plates with pickles, herbs, or a bright dip rather than eating the protein alone.
worth_knowing: This is a practical traveler order: easy to understand, filling, and still Vietnamese in seasoning.

english_translation: Rice with braised pork and eggs
at_a_glance: Cơm thịt kho trứng is rice with caramel-braised pork and egg, usually in a salty-sweet fish-sauce braise. The rice is there to soak up the dark sauce.
usually_includes: rice | braised pork | egg | caramel fish-sauce braise | pickles or greens
good_to_know: This is the rice-plate version of a family-style braise. Ask for more rice rather than more sauce if the flavor is too intense.
common_options: extra rice | extra egg | more braising liquid | less fatty pork
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm thịt kho trứng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of rice with braised pork and eggs.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum tit kaw choong
what_it_is: Cơm thịt kho trứng is rice with pork belly or pork pieces braised with eggs in coconut-water fish-sauce caramel. It is sweet-salty, homey, and made for spooning over rice.
how_to_enjoy: Break the egg into the rice, spoon a little braising liquid over the grains, and balance the richness with pickles or greens if they come with the plate.
how_locals_order: Order cơm thịt kho trứng when you want a homestyle pork-and-egg rice plate. Ask for extra rice or more egg if you want the sweet-salty braise to go further.
worth_knowing: Thịt kho trứng is strongly tied to Vietnamese home cooking and Tết memories, so it can feel more like family food than street food.
traveler_caution: Contains pork, egg, and fish sauce.

english_translation: Rice with caramelized fish in clay pot
at_a_glance: Cơm cá kho tộ is rice with clay-pot caramelized fish. The dark fish-sauce caramel is meant to season the rice.
usually_includes: rice | caramelized fish | fish-sauce caramel | black pepper | pickles or greens
good_to_know: Ask about bones if you prefer easier fish pieces. The fish-sauce caramel braise should be intense, not mild.
common_options: fried egg | extra rice | less fish-sauce caramel braise | extra pickles
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm cá kho tộ.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of rice with caramelized fish in clay pot.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum kah kaw toh
what_it_is: Cơm cá kho tộ is the rice-plate version of cá kho tộ, fish braised in fish sauce, caramelized sugar, and pepper.
how_to_enjoy: Use plain rice to soften the salty-sweet sauce. Add pickles or greens for contrast.
how_locals_order: Order cơm cá kho tộ when you want clay-pot caramel fish with rice. Ask about bones before the plate lands, and ask for extra rice if you like soaking up the fish-sauce caramel juices.
worth_knowing: This is a comfort-food order, especially in southern-style meals where braised fish and rice belong together. In Vietnam, rice plates are everyday meals shaped by broken rice, scallion oil, pickles, fish-sauce caramel, and quick street-service habits.
traveler_caution: May contain fish bones and fish sauce.

at_a_glance: Cơm tôm rim is rice with shrimp simmered in a sticky salty-sweet fish-sauce caramel. It is small, punchy, and rice-hungry.
usually_includes: rice | caramelized shrimp | fish-sauce glaze | garlic | pickles or greens
good_to_know: Rim means simmered down until the fish-sauce caramel braise clings. This is not a saucy curry or soup.
common_options: extra rice | ask about shells | less spicy | extra pickles
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm tôm rim.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of rice with caramelized shrimp.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum tom reem
what_it_is: Cơm tôm rim is rice with shrimp simmered until glossy in a sweet-salty fish-sauce caramel. The shrimp may be shell-on, which gives the glaze deeper seafood flavor.
how_to_enjoy: Spoon the shrimp glaze into the rice a little at a time, and check whether the shells are meant to be peeled. Pickles or cucumber help cut the sweetness.
how_locals_order: Order cơm tôm rim when you want a savory shrimp rice plate. Ask còn vỏ không if you want to know whether shells remain, and ask for extra rice if the glaze is rich.
worth_knowing: Rim means simmered down until concentrated; on shrimp it creates a sticky, salty-sweet coating that Vietnamese rice is perfect for catching.
traveler_caution: Contains shrimp and fish sauce.

at_a_glance: Cơm chiên dương châu is Dương Châu fried rice, usually with egg, sausage or ham, shrimp, peas, carrot, and scallion.
usually_includes: fried rice grains | egg | sausage or ham | shrimp | peas and carrots
good_to_know: This mixed fried rice can include shrimp and pork sausage or ham, so ask first if shellfish or pork matters.
common_options: less oil | no shrimp | no pork | extra egg
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm chiên dương châu.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of yangzhou fried rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum chee-en yuhng chow
what_it_is: Cơm chiên dương châu is Yangzhou-style fried rice in Vietnamese restaurant language, usually with egg, sausage or ham, shrimp, peas, carrots, and scallions.
