how_to_enjoy: Eat it hot while the grains stay separate and lightly smoky from the wok. Add chili or soy-lime seasoning sparingly so the egg and sausage flavor stays clear.
how_locals_order: Order cơm chiên dương châu when you want a mixed fried rice plate. Ask for no shrimp, no pork sausage, or less oil before the wok starts if those matter.
worth_knowing: This is a familiar Chinese-Vietnamese restaurant order, useful when traveling with people who want something simple but still local to the menu style.

at_a_glance: Cơm chiên hải sản is seafood fried rice, usually with shrimp, squid, egg, scallion, and wok-tossed grains.
usually_includes: fried rice | shrimp or squid | egg | scallions | peas or vegetables
good_to_know: Good seafood fried rice should taste wok-hot, lightly smoky, and dotted with sweet seafood. Use chili or soy if offered, but the rice itself should carry the flavor.
common_options: less oil | less spicy | ask about shellfish | extra egg
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm chiên hải sản.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of seafood fried rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum chee-en high sahn
what_it_is: Cơm chiên hải sản is seafood fried rice with shrimp, squid, fish cake, egg, scallions, and wok aroma. It should be savory and briny, not wet.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it hot so the rice grains stay separate and the seafood stays tender. Ask what seafood is included if shellfish is a concern.
how_locals_order: Order cơm chiên hải sản for a seafood-heavy fried rice. Ask ít dầu, ít cay, or no shellfish before the wok starts.
worth_knowing: Hải sản can vary by shop, so the same name may mean shrimp and squid at one place and a broader seafood mix at another.
traveler_caution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.

at_a_glance: Cơm chiên gà is chicken fried rice, usually with egg, chicken, scallion, vegetables, and soy-seasoned rice.
usually_includes: fried rice | chicken | egg | scallions | vegetables
good_to_know: Order this when you want something straightforward and filling. The best versions taste of hot wok, egg, chicken, and scallion rather than a separate condiment.
common_options: less oil | no chili | extra egg | extra chicken
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm chiên gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of chicken fried rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum chee-en gah
what_it_is: Cơm chiên gà is chicken fried rice with egg, scallions, garlic, and small pieces of chicken. It is a steady, filling order when you want familiar flavors in a Vietnamese shop.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it while the rice is hot and separate-grained. A little chili or soy-lime seasoning is enough; the chicken and wok aroma should stay in front.
how_locals_order: Order cơm chiên gà when you want a simple chicken fried rice. Ask ít dầu, không cay, or thêm trứng before the wok starts.
worth_knowing: Fried rice in Vietnam is often cooked quickly to order, so oil level, chili, and egg are the easiest adjustments to request.

at_a_glance: Cơm chiên bò is beef fried rice, usually with wok-tossed rice, egg, beef, scallion, and vegetables.
usually_includes: fried rice | beef | egg | scallions | garlic or onion
good_to_know: The beef and egg should season the rice as it fries. Add chili or soy only if you want extra punch after tasting the first few bites.
common_options: less oil | no onion | extra egg | less spicy
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm chiên bò.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of beef fried rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum chee-en baw
what_it_is: Cơm chiên bò is beef fried rice with egg, scallions, garlic, and wok-seared beef pieces. The best versions are dry enough that the grains stay distinct.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it hot from the wok and use chili lightly. The beef, egg, and garlic should season the rice so each grain tastes savory on its own.
how_locals_order: Order cơm chiên bò when you want fried rice with beef rather than a sauced beef plate. Ask for less oil, no onion, or extra egg before cooking.
worth_knowing: This is a practical Vietnamese rice-shop order: quick, filling, and easy to adjust for oil, chili, onion, or egg.

at_a_glance: Cơm chiên trứng is egg fried rice, usually with egg, scallion, garlic, and grains fried until separate.
usually_includes: fried rice | egg | scallions | garlic | pepper
good_to_know: This is a simple wok-rice order, often chosen when you want something quick, hot, and not too heavy. The egg should coat the grains lightly.
common_options: less oil | extra egg | no chili | extra scallions
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm chiên trứng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of egg fried rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum chee-en choong
what_it_is: Cơm chiên trứng is egg fried rice, usually just rice, egg, scallions, garlic, and wok seasoning. Its simplicity makes texture important.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it while the grains are hot and separate, with egg coating the rice instead of clumping. Add chili only if you want heat, not because the dish needs rescuing.
how_locals_order: Order cơm chiên trứng when you want the simplest fried rice. Ask ít dầu, thêm trứng, or không cay before the wok starts.
worth_knowing: This can be a safe fallback order for travelers, but a good shop still makes it fragrant with egg, scallion, and hot wok breath.

english_translation: Fried rice with beef and pickled mustard greens
at_a_glance: Cơm rang dưa bò is fried rice with beef and pickled mustard greens, usually with egg, garlic, scallions, and a tangy wok flavor.
usually_includes: fried rice | beef | pickled mustard greens | egg | scallions
good_to_know: Dưa chua, pickled mustard greens, gives the rice its northern sour-savory snap; ask for extra dưa if you like that brightness.
common_options: less oil | extra pickled greens | no chili | extra egg
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm rang dưa bò.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of fried rice with beef and pickled mustard greens.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum rang yoo-uh baw
what_it_is: Cơm rang dưa bò is northern-style fried rice with beef and dưa chua, pickled mustard greens. The sour greens cut through the beef and make the rice taste brighter.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it hot so the tangy dưa chua and beef stay lively. The pickled greens are the point, so taste before adding chili.
how_locals_order: Order cơm rang dưa bò when you want beef fried rice with a northern sour kick. Ask for less oil, no chili, or extra pickled mustard greens before cooking.
worth_knowing: Dưa bò is a useful phrase: it points to beef paired with pickled mustard greens, a beloved northern comfort flavor.

at_a_glance: Cơm niêu is clay-pot rice, usually with crisp rice edges, fluffy center, and shared savory dishes.
usually_includes: clay-pot rice | crisp rice edges | steamed rice center | shared side dishes | scallion oil optional
good_to_know: Ask what comes with the clay-pot rice. Some places serve a full shared set, while others expect you to choose braised fish, vegetables, or soup separately.
common_options: ask what comes with it | extra shared dish | vegetables | braised fish
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm niêu.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of clay pot rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum nee-ew
what_it_is: Cơm niêu is clay-pot rice, served hot with a crisp bottom or edges and meant to accompany shared dishes. The rice itself is the attraction.
how_to_enjoy: Scrape some crisp rice edge with the soft rice, then eat it alongside braised fish, vegetables, or soup. Order shared dishes if the menu lists cơm niêu as plain rice.
how_locals_order: Order cơm niêu when you want the clay-pot rice experience. Ask what dishes come with it, because some shops sell the rice alone and others serve a full set.
worth_knowing: The joy is texture: soft rice in the middle, toasted edges near the pot, and family-style dishes around it.

english_translation: Clay pot rice with caramelized fish
at_a_glance: Cơm niêu cá kho pairs clay-pot rice with caramelized fish. The fish sauce, caramel, pepper, and rice are the point: salty-sweet sauce against plain rice.
usually_includes: clay-pot rice | caramelized fish | fish-sauce caramel | pepper | pickles or greens
good_to_know: Cơm niêu means clay-pot rice, often prized for hot fluffy rice and crisp edges. Watch for fish bones in cá kho.
common_options: extra rice | ask about bones | less pepper | share size
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cơm niêu cá kho.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of clay pot rice with caramelized fish.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kum nee-ew kah kaw
what_it_is: Cơm niêu cá kho is clay-pot rice with caramelized fish. It puts two comforts together: hot rice and fish braised in fish-sauce caramel.
how_to_enjoy: Use the rice to soften the salty-sweet fish sauce caramel. Ask about bones before ordering if you want an easier plate.
how_locals_order: Cơm niêu cá kho is a clay-pot rice order, good for sharing with braised or salty dishes. Ask whether the crispy rice is served at the table, and order extra rice if the table has strong fish-sauce caramel dishes.
worth_knowing: Cơm niêu means clay-pot rice; cá kho is the braised fish. Together, they read more like a sit-down comfort meal than a quick rice plate. In Vietnam, rice plates are everyday meals shaped by broken rice, scallion oil, pickles, fish-sauce caramel, and quick street-service habits.
traveler_caution: May contain fish bones and fish sauce.

at_a_glance: Xôi gà is sticky rice with chicken, usually with shredded chicken, fried shallots, herbs, and sometimes chicken sauce.
usually_includes: sticky rice | chicken | fried shallots | savory topping
good_to_know: This is often a morning or takeaway packet. Fried shallots, chicken shreds, and warm sticky rice matter more than a separate dip.
common_options: extra chicken | extra fried shallots | less spicy | pack to go
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần xôi gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of sticky rice with chicken.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn soy gah
what_it_is: Xôi gà is sticky rice topped with chicken, often shredded or chopped, with fried shallots, scallion oil, herbs, and sometimes chicken gravy or soy-chili seasoning.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it warm so the sticky rice stays soft and the fried shallots stay fragrant. Mix chicken through the rice gradually rather than treating it like a separate side.
how_locals_order: Order xôi gà for a filling breakfast or snack. Ask for extra fried shallots, less chili, or more chicken before the vendor closes the packet.
worth_knowing: Xôi stalls are a major morning rhythm in Vietnam; the rice is dense, portable, and often wrapped for takeaway.

english_translation: Sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots
at_a_glance: Xôi xéo is yellow sticky rice with mung bean, usually with fried shallots, chicken fat or oil, and optional toppings.
usually_includes: sticky rice | mung bean paste | fried shallots | scallion oil | salted seasoning
good_to_know: Ask for không cay if you want Xôi xéo without added chili.
common_options: extra fried shallots | extra mung bean | pack to go | less oil
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần xôi xéo.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn soy say-oh
what_it_is: Xôi xéo is sticky rice topped with shaved mung bean paste, fried shallots, and oil. It is nutty, savory, and especially associated with northern breakfasts.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it warm while the mung bean is soft and the fried shallots are crisp. Mix gently so every bite gets rice, bean, and shallot.
how_locals_order: Order xôi xéo at morning stalls when you want a northern-style sticky rice packet. Ask for extra fried shallots or pack to go before it is wrapped.
worth_knowing: The name is a Hanoi breakfast signal for many Vietnamese people, even though you can find versions elsewhere.

at_a_glance: Xôi mặn is savory sticky rice with assorted toppings such as Chinese sausage, shredded pork, egg, fried shallots, and pâté-like spreads depending on the vendor.
usually_includes: sticky rice | Chinese sausage | egg or pâté | pork floss | fried shallots
good_to_know: It is dense for its size. Treat it as a portable breakfast or snack that eats more like a small meal.
common_options: extra egg | no pâté | no pork | pack to go
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần xôi mặn.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of savory sticky rice.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn soy mahn
what_it_is: Xôi mặn is savory sticky rice loaded with toppings such as Chinese sausage, shredded pork, egg, pâté, pork floss, scallion oil, and fried shallots.
how_to_enjoy: Mix the rich toppings through the sticky rice while it is warm. A small amount of chili or soy seasoning is enough because the toppings are already salty and savory.
how_locals_order: Order xôi mặn when you want a loaded savory sticky-rice packet. Ask what toppings are included, then request no pâté, no pork, or extra egg before wrapping.
worth_knowing: Mặn means savory or salty, which separates this from sweet xôi orders on breakfast menus.
traveler_caution: May include pork sausage, pâté, or egg depending on the vendor.

at_a_glance: Xôi lạp xưởng is sticky rice with Chinese sausage, usually with sweet-savory lạp xưởng, fried shallots, and sticky grains.
usually_includes: sticky rice | pork | fried shallots | savory topping
good_to_know: May contain pork.
common_options: extra sausage | extra fried shallots | pack to go | less oil
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần xôi lạp xưởng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of sticky rice with Chinese sausage.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn soy lap swoong
what_it_is: Xôi lạp xưởng is sticky rice topped with sweet-savory Chinese-style sausage. The sausage fat perfumes the rice, especially when the packet is still warm.
how_to_enjoy: Slice or mix the sausage through the sticky rice so the sweet fat seasons the grains. Fried shallots or scallion oil add crunch and aroma.
how_locals_order: Order xôi lạp xưởng when you want sticky rice with a sweet sausage bite. Ask for extra fried shallots or pack to go before it is wrapped.
worth_knowing: Lạp xưởng is a useful menu word for Chinese-style sausage, common in Vietnamese breakfasts, rice plates, and fried rice.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

english_translation: Sticky rice dumpling with mung bean and pork
at_a_glance: Xôi khúc is sticky rice dumpling with khúc leaves, usually with mung bean, pork filling, and herbal green rice.
usually_includes: sticky rice | khúc leaf dough | mung bean | pork filling | fried shallots optional
good_to_know: May contain pork.
common_options: pack to go | ask about pork | extra fried shallots | one piece
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần xôi khúc.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of sticky rice dumpling with mung bean and pork.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn soy khook
what_it_is: Xôi khúc is sticky rice wrapped around a khúc-leaf dumpling with mung bean and pork inside. It is warm, dense, herbal, and especially loved as a northern breakfast.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it warm and break into the center so the mung bean, pork, and herbal dough mix with the sticky rice. It is filling, so one portion can be plenty.
how_locals_order: Order xôi khúc early in the day if you see it at a stall. Ask whether it has pork if you are avoiding meat; the filling is often hidden until you bite in.
worth_knowing: In northern Vietnam, khúc leaf gives this sticky-rice dumpling its herbal character, making it feel different from ordinary xôi packets.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Xôi bắp is sticky rice with corn, usually with mung bean, fried shallot, sugar or savory toppings.
usually_includes: sticky rice | corn | mung bean | fried shallots | sugar or coconut optional
good_to_know: Xôi bắp can lean lightly sweet or lightly savory depending on the seller. Look for chewy corn, sticky rice, mung bean, fried shallots, and a sesame-sugar or coconut finish.
common_options: less sugar | extra fried shallots | extra mung bean | pack to go
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần xôi bắp.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of sticky rice with corn.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn soy bap
what_it_is: Xôi bắp is sticky rice with corn, mung bean, fried shallots, and sometimes sugar or coconut depending on the stall. It can lean savory, sweet, or both.
how_to_enjoy: Taste before adding sugar or chili because stalls vary. The best bites have chewy corn, soft mung bean, and fragrant fried shallots together.
how_locals_order: Order xôi bắp when you want a lighter, corn-sweet sticky rice. Ask for less sugar, extra fried shallots, or pack to go before the packet is closed.
worth_knowing: Bắp means corn in southern Vietnamese usage; this is a useful word for reading snacks and dessert menus.

at_a_glance: Bánh mì đặc biệt is the house-special sandwich, stacking the French-Vietnamese bánh mì story with pâté, cold cuts, pickles, cucumber, cilantro, chili, and seasoning.
usually_includes: baguette | pâté | Vietnamese cold cuts | pickles and cucumber | cilantro and chili
good_to_know: Fillings vary by shop. Ask what meats are inside if pork, pâté, or processed meat matters, and keep the pickles unless you truly dislike sour crunch.
common_options: no chili | extra pâté | extra pickles | no pork
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ổ bánh mì đặc biệt.
quick_say_english: I’d like one special bánh mì.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht oh bahn mee dak bee-et
what_it_is: Bánh mì đặc biệt is the “special” mixed-meat bánh mì, usually layered with pâté, Vietnamese cold cuts, pork floss or ham, đồ chua pickles, cucumber, cilantro, chili, and Maggi-style seasoning.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it soon, while the bread is crisp and the pâté is still rich against the pickles. The fun is how many layers fit into a loaf that still feels fresh and quick.
how_locals_order: Order bánh mì đặc biệt when you want the fully loaded house version. Ask what meats are inside if you avoid pork, and say không ớt for no chili before the vendor closes it.
worth_knowing: Đặc biệt means special, so each stall’s version tells you what that vendor is proud of. It also shows why bánh mì lasted: French-influenced bread became a flexible Vietnamese street-food platform.
traveler_caution: Often contains pork and pâté.

at_a_glance: The classic mixed-meat bánh mì: French-introduced bread made Vietnamese with pâté, pork, đồ chua pickles, cilantro, cucumber, chili, and street-cart speed.
usually_includes: baguette | pork | pickled vegetables | cilantro | chili optional
good_to_know: If you do not eat pâté or pork liver, ask before ordering.
common_options: no chili | extra pickles | extra pâté | less sauce
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ổ bánh mì thịt.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bánh mì thịt.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht oh bahn mee tit
what_it_is: Bánh mì thịt is the everyday meat sandwich many visitors imagine first, but it is also a compact food history: baguette and pâté meeting Vietnamese pork, herbs, pickled carrot and daikon, and Maggi-style seasoning.
how_to_enjoy: Point to the fillings you want if the cart has a glass case. Eat it soon after ordering so the crust stays crisp, the pâté is warm, and the pickles still cut through the pork.
how_locals_order: Order bánh mì thịt for a pork bánh mì, then say no chili or extra pickles before the vendor adds the final seasoning. Locals keep coming back because it works as breakfast, a workday snack, or a meal you can carry on a motorbike.
worth_knowing: Bánh mì became beloved because Vietnam transformed a colonial-era baguette into democratic street food: affordable, fast, layered, and unmistakably local once herbs, pickles, chili, and pork went inside.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: A smoky grilled-pork bánh mì with sweet-savory marinade, fresh herbs, cucumber, pickles, and chili tucked into a crisp loaf.
usually_includes: baguette | pork | pickled vegetables | cilantro | chili optional
good_to_know: Ask for less chili if you want to focus on the lemongrass sweetness.
common_options: no chili | extra pickles | extra grilled pork | less sauce
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ổ bánh mì thịt nướng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one grilled pork bánh mì.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht oh bahn mee tit noong
what_it_is: Bánh mì thịt nướng centers on charred slices or strips of marinated pork, usually fragrant with lemongrass, fish sauce, garlic, and sugar, balanced by cilantro and đồ chua.
how_to_enjoy: Choose it when you smell meat grilling nearby; that little bit of smoke is the point. It is great for lunch or a late-night snack after the grill has built up flavor.
how_locals_order: Order bánh mì thịt nướng when you want grilled pork rather than cold cuts. Ask for no chili early, and keep the pickles because they cut the smoky sweetness.
worth_knowing: Thịt nướng is a core southern Vietnamese flavor, also found over rice noodles and broken rice. In bánh mì form, it shows how Vietnam took the French-influenced loaf and filled it with local grill smoke, fish sauce, herbs, and đồ chua.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Bánh mì heo quay is roast-pork bánh mì, bringing crackling pork into Vietnam’s French-influenced street sandwich with pickles, cucumber, cilantro, and chili.
usually_includes: baguette | roast pork with crackling | pickles | cucumber | cilantro
good_to_know: May contain pork.
common_options: no chili | extra pickles | extra roast pork | less sauce
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ổ bánh mì heo quay.
quick_say_english: I’d like one roast pork bánh mì.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht oh bahn mee heh-oh kway
what_it_is: Bánh mì heo quay makes roast pork with crisp skin the star. The best bite has crackling, rich pork, sharp pickles, cucumber, cilantro, and a little chili if you want heat.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it soon so the crackling stays crisp against the bread. Ask for no chili before the vendor adds chili or spicy seasoning.
how_locals_order: Order bánh mì heo quay when you want crunch from roast pork skin. Ask for extra pickles or no chili early, because bánh mì stalls move quickly and the sandwich is assembled in seconds.
worth_knowing: Heo quay means roast pork; inside bánh mì, it shows Vietnam’s habit of adapting the loaf to local appetites. Crackling, herbs, and đồ chua make it feel more Vietnamese than a simple roast-pork sandwich.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: A cool, savory bánh mì that puts Vietnam’s smooth chả lụa pork sausage into a French-influenced loaf with herbs and pickles.
usually_includes: baguette | pork | pickled vegetables | cilantro | chili optional
good_to_know: Useful phrase: ask for no chili if you are heat-sensitive.
common_options: no chili | extra pâté | extra pickles | toasted bread
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ổ bánh mì chả lụa.
quick_say_english: I’d like one chả lụa bánh mì.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht oh bahn mee chah loo-uh
what_it_is: Bánh mì chả lụa is the deli-counter side of the Vietnamese sandwich: pale slices of steamed pork sausage, pâté or butter, cucumber, cilantro, chili, and đồ chua in a loaf that should shatter lightly when you bite it.
how_to_enjoy: It is best as a quick breakfast or train-station snack. Ask for chili only if you want heat, then eat it while the bread is still warm and the sausage is cool and springy.
how_locals_order: Order bánh mì chả lụa when you want smooth Vietnamese pork sausage instead of grilled meat. Ask for no chili, extra pickles, or extra pâté before the bread is closed.
worth_knowing: Chả lụa appears at family meals, holiday platters, and lunch counters, so this sandwich brings a familiar Vietnamese sausage into the bánh mì story instead of only copying a French deli sandwich.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Bánh mì ốp la is a breakfast bánh mì with sunny eggs, herbs, cucumber, pickles, chili, and Maggi-style soy seasoning, often cooked on a small street griddle.
usually_includes: baguette | egg | pickled vegetables | cilantro | chili optional
good_to_know: Ask for không cay if you want the egg sandwich without chili.
common_options: no chili | egg well-done | extra egg | extra pickles
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ổ bánh mì ốp la.
quick_say_english: I’d like one fried egg bánh mì.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht oh bahn mee awp lah
what_it_is: Bánh mì ốp la is a fried-egg bánh mì, often served with runny eggs, pâté or soy seasoning, cucumber, pickles, cilantro, and chili. It is a beloved breakfast order.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it early in the day when the eggs are hot and the bread is just warmed. If you like runny yolk, stay close to the stall and eat before it soaks too far into the loaf.
how_locals_order: Order bánh mì ốp la for breakfast-style comfort. Ask for no chili or egg well-done before the egg and bread are finished.
worth_knowing: Ốp la shows how Vietnamese breakfast can be quick but still vivid: French-influenced bread, local herbs, pickles, seasoning, and a hot egg all in one hand-held meal for people heading to school or work.

at_a_glance: A chicken bánh mì with shredded or grilled gà, crisp pickles, herbs, and bright chili, pâté, or Maggi-style seasoning inside Vietnam's famous airy baguette.
usually_includes: baguette | chicken | pickled vegetables | cilantro | chili optional
good_to_know: Ask whether it has pâté if you avoid pork liver.
common_options: no chili | extra pâté | extra pickles | toasted bread
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ổ bánh mì gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one chicken bánh mì.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht oh bahn mee gah
what_it_is: Bánh mì gà usually means chicken layered into a Vietnamese baguette with cucumber, cilantro, pickled carrot and daikon, and a swipe of pâté, chili, or Maggi-style soy seasoning depending on the stall.
how_to_enjoy: Look for a vendor turning over sandwiches quickly so the bread stays fresh. It is a good first bánh mì if you want something lighter than pork but still full of herb-and-pickle snap.
how_locals_order: Order bánh mì gà when you want chicken instead of pork. Ask for no chili, extra pickles, or less mayonnaise-style spread before the sandwich is closed.
worth_knowing: Chicken bánh mì shows how the sandwich stayed alive by adapting. The French-influenced loaf remains, but the filling can shift to chicken while the Vietnamese identity comes from herbs, đồ chua, chili, and quick street service.

at_a_glance: Bánh mì bò kho is Vietnamese beef stew served with crisp baguette for dipping. The stew is warm, aromatic, and rich with beef, carrots, and gentle spice.
usually_includes: baguette | beef stew | carrots | herbs | spiced broth
good_to_know: This is not a filled sandwich. Tear the bread and dip it into the broth, then use herbs, lime, or chili to brighten the stew.
common_options: extra bread | less spicy | extra herbs | share size
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bò kho bánh mì.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of beef stew with bread.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn baw kaw banh mee
what_it_is: Bánh mì bò kho is Vietnamese beef stew served with bread for dipping. The bowl brings tender beef, carrots, warm spice, herbs, and broth that the baguette is meant to catch.
how_to_enjoy: Tear the bread and dip it into the stew while the broth is hot. Add herbs, lime, or chili gradually so the warm spice stays balanced.
how_locals_order: Bánh mì bò kho is ordered as stew plus bread, not a normal sandwich. Ask for extra bread if you like dipping, and ask less spicy before the bò kho broth is ladled.
worth_knowing: This order shows another side of bánh mì: bread as a tool for broth, not just a sandwich. Bò kho itself is a Vietnamese comfort stew with beef, carrots, and aromatics.

at_a_glance: Bánh mì pate carries the bánh mì story in one loaf: French-style pâté and bread reshaped by Vietnam’s herbs, pickles, chili, and street-food pace.
usually_includes: baguette | pâté | pickles | cilantro | chili optional
good_to_know: Pâté is usually liver-based. If that flavor is not for you, choose grilled pork, chicken, or egg, but try to notice how the pickles and herbs are designed to balance the richness.
common_options: no chili | extra pickles | less pâté | toasted bread
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ổ bánh mì pate.
quick_say_english: I’d like one pâté bánh mì.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht oh bahn mee pah-tay
what_it_is: Bánh mì pate is a Vietnamese baguette sandwich where liver pâté gives the rich, silky base. The Vietnamese part is just as important: sharp đồ chua pickles, cilantro, cucumber, chili, and a light crackly loaf keep the pâté from feeling heavy.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it while the bread is warm so the pâté softens into the crumb. Extra pickles are not decoration; their sour crunch is what makes the rich French-influenced spread feel Vietnamese.
how_locals_order: Order bánh mì pate when you want pâté to lead, then ask for extra pickles or no chili before the vendor closes the bread. Locals still eat it because it is fast, cheap, portable, and satisfying for breakfast or a street snack.
worth_knowing: Bánh mì grew from French colonial bread and pâté, then Vietnam made it its own by using lighter baguettes, herbs, đồ chua, chili, and made-to-order street carts. The pâté version keeps that history visible.
traveler_caution: Contains liver pâté.

at_a_glance: Bánh mì xíu mại is a meatball bánh mì, often saucier than the cold-cut versions. The pork meatballs and tomato-like sauce make the bread softer and more comforting.
usually_includes: baguette | pork meatballs | tomato-rich xíu mại sauce | pickles | cilantro
good_to_know: This one can be messy in a good way. Eat it sitting down if the bread is filled with tomato-pork xíu mại sauce rather than dry toppings.
common_options: no chili | extra bread | extra pickles | less spicy
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ổ bánh mì xíu mại.
quick_say_english: I’d like one xíu mại bánh mì.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht oh bahn mee see-ew my
what_it_is: Bánh mì xíu mại is a meatball bánh mì, often with soft pork meatballs in tomato-forward xíu mại gravy, plus herbs, pickles, and bread for soaking up the juices.
how_to_enjoy: Use the bread to catch the tomato-pork juices, and eat before the baguette softens too much. Ask for no chili before the meatballs are spooned in.
how_locals_order: Order bánh mì xíu mại when you want the saucy meatball version. Ask for extra bread, no chili, or xíu mại in a bowl if the shop offers it.
worth_knowing: Xíu mại in Vietnam usually points to soft pork meatballs, often tomato-bright and spoonable rather than dim sum. With bánh mì, it turns the French-influenced loaf into a Vietnamese comfort food for soaking, scooping, and quick breakfasts.
traveler_caution: Usually contains pork.

at_a_glance: Bánh mì chay is vegetarian bánh mì, usually with tofu, mushrooms, mock meat, pickles, cucumber, cilantro, chili, and vegetarian seasoning.
usually_includes: baguette | tofu or mock meat | mushrooms optional | pickles and cucumber | cilantro
good_to_know: Chay means vegetarian, but strict vegetarians should still ask about fish sauce, egg, and dairy because Maggi-style soy seasoning, chili, or pâté spreads vary.
common_options: vegetarian | no fish sauce | no chili | extra pickles
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một ổ bánh mì chay.
quick_say_english: I’d like one vegetarian bánh mì.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht oh bahn mee chai
what_it_is: Bánh mì chay keeps the crisp baguette, pickles, herbs, and chili of bánh mì but uses tofu, mushrooms, or mock meat instead of pork. Strict vegetarians should still ask about fish sauce or pâté at mixed stalls.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it fresh while the bread is crisp. If you are strict vegetarian, ask about nước mắm and pâté before the sandwich is assembled.
how_locals_order: Order bánh mì chay and repeat chay if the stall also sells meat sandwiches. Ask không nước mắm and không pate if you need the vegetarian boundary to be clear.
worth_knowing: Bánh mì chay shows the sandwich’s Vietnamese flexibility: the French-influenced loaf stays, but Buddhist vegetarian habits and tofu or mushroom fillings make it work on meat-free days.
traveler_caution: Ask about fish sauce, egg, or dairy if strict vegetarian.

at_a_glance: Bánh bao is a soft steamed bun with a sealed savory filling inside slightly sweet dough. It is warm, portable, and closer to a filled bun than a sandwich.
usually_includes: steamed bun | savory filling | soft dough | egg optional | pork optional
good_to_know: Do not ask for this toasted like bánh mì. The point is the soft steamed dough and hidden filling.
common_options: warm | takeaway | ask what filling | no egg
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một cái bánh bao.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of steamed bun.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht kai bahn bow
what_it_is: Bánh bao is a Vietnamese steamed bun, often with pork, egg, mushroom, or other savory filling sealed inside fluffy dough.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it warm and split carefully if you want to check the filling first. The bun can be more filling than it looks.
how_locals_order: Bánh bao is a warm takeaway bun order; ask what filling is inside if the tray is mixed. Locals buy it for a quick breakfast or snack, so ask for it warmed before leaving.
worth_knowing: Bánh bao sits in Vietnam’s bakery and snack world, but it is steamed rather than baked or toasted.
traveler_caution: May contain pork and egg.

at_a_glance: Bánh bao xá xíu is a steamed bun filled with sweet-savory barbecue pork. The soft dough and saucy pork are the appeal.
usually_includes: steamed bun | xá xíu pork | sweet-salty glaze | soft dough
good_to_know: Xá xíu means char siu-style pork. This is a pork bun, not a crisp baguette sandwich.
common_options: warm | takeaway | extra filling | share size
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một cái bánh bao xá xíu.
quick_say_english: I’d like one char siu steamed bun.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht kai bahn bow sah see-ew
what_it_is: Bánh bao xá xíu is a soft steamed bun filled with sweet-salty barbecue pork.
how_to_enjoy: Eat warm while the dough is soft. If pork is a no, choose bánh bao chay instead.
how_locals_order: Order bánh bao xá xíu when you want the barbecue pork steamed-bun version. Ask whether it has egg inside if you care about the filling.
worth_knowing: Xá xíu reflects Chinese-Vietnamese roast-pork flavor inside a Vietnamese snack-counter bun.
traveler_caution: Contains pork.

at_a_glance: Bánh bao chay is a vegetarian steamed bun, usually filled with mushrooms, vegetables, tofu, or mock meat depending on the shop.
usually_includes: steamed bun | vegetarian filling | mushrooms or vegetables | soft dough
good_to_know: Chay signals vegetarian, but ask about egg or dairy if strict. The bun should be steamed, soft, and warm.
common_options: warm | takeaway | ask about egg | extra filling
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một cái bánh bao chay.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of vegetarian steamed bun.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht kai bahn bow chai
what_it_is: Bánh bao chay is the vegetarian version of a steamed bun: soft dough around a savory plant-based filling.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it warm and check the filling if strict vegetarian details matter.
how_locals_order: Bánh bao chay is a warm takeaway bun order; ask what filling is inside if the tray is mixed. Locals buy it for a quick breakfast or snack, so ask for it warmed before leaving.
worth_knowing: Chay is the useful menu word here. It tells you this is not the pork-and-egg steamed bun lane. In Vietnam, bánh bao belongs to the snack-counter world: soft steamed dough, hidden filling, and quick takeaway warmth rather than crisp baguette texture.
traveler_caution: Ask about egg or dairy if strict vegetarian.

at_a_glance: Bánh tiêu is a hollow sesame donut with a crisp outside, airy middle, and gentle sweetness. It is a street snack, not a sandwich.
usually_includes: fried sesame dough | hollow center | light sweetness
good_to_know: Freshness matters most. The outside should still have a little crackle, while the center stays light and hollow.
common_options: freshly fried | takeaway | share size
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một cái bánh tiêu.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of hollow sesame donut.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht kai bahn tee-ew
what_it_is: Bánh tiêu is a hollow sesame donut with a crisp outside, airy middle, and gentle sweetness. It is a street snack or bakery bite rather than a filled dessert.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it fresh if possible, while the outside still crackles. It is best simple: sesame aroma, light sweetness, and warm dough.
how_locals_order: Bánh tiêu is best ordered freshly fried, when the sesame shell is still airy and warm. Buy a few to share, and eat it soon because the hollow crunch fades quickly.
worth_knowing: Bánh tiêu belongs to Vietnam’s everyday snack world, where fried dough, sesame, and portable bakery treats sit beside savory bread orders.

at_a_glance: Bánh patê sô is a savory puff pastry with flaky layers and seasoned filling. It belongs to Vietnam’s bakery-counter snack lane.
usually_includes: puff pastry | savory filling | buttery layers
good_to_know: It is best warm, when the pastry is flaky and the filling is aromatic. Treat it as a quick bakery snack, not a bánh mì.
common_options: warm | takeaway | share size
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một cái bánh patê sô.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of savory puff pastry.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht kai bahn pah-tay soh
what_it_is: Bánh patê sô is a savory puff pastry with flaky layers and seasoned filling. It is familiar in shape but belongs naturally to Vietnamese bakery counters.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it warm for the best flaky texture. It works as a quick bakery snack rather than a full sandwich.
how_locals_order: Bánh patê sô is a bakery-style order, so ask whether it is warm from the oven. Locals treat the flaky pastry as a quick snack; share size makes sense if you are tasting several items.
worth_knowing: Patê sô reflects Vietnam’s bakery culture, where flaky pastry and savory fillings sit beside bánh mì and sweet snacks.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Gỏi cuốn are fresh spring rolls wrapped in rice paper with herbs, noodles, and a light filling. They are cool, clean, and great as a starter or snack.
usually_includes: rice paper | fresh spring rolls | rice vermicelli | herbs | peanut sauce or nước chấm
good_to_know: The peanut-hoisin dip or nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip changes the flavor. Peanut sauce is richer; nước chấm is lighter, salty, sweet, and bright.
common_options: peanut sauce | nước chấm | more herbs | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần gỏi cuốn.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of fresh spring rolls.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn goy kwun
what_it_is: Gỏi cuốn are fresh rice-paper rolls with herbs, noodles, and a light filling such as shrimp, pork, or tofu. They are cool, clean, and a gentle way into Vietnamese flavors.
how_to_enjoy: Dip, do not soak. Peanut sauce is richer; nước chấm is lighter, salty-sweet, and brighter.
how_locals_order: Gỏi cuốn is ordered by the plate or by the roll, then matched with the dip you want. If peanuts are a problem, ask before choosing peanut-hoisin; nước chấm is the brighter fish-sauce-lime option.
worth_knowing: These rolls are often called fresh spring rolls in English, which helps distinguish them from fried chả giò or nem rán. In Vietnam, snacks like this depend on rice paper, herbs, peanut-hoisin dip or nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip, and stall texture; the same name can shift by region.

usually_includes: rice paper | shrimp and pork | rice vermicelli | herbs | peanut sauce or nước chấm
good_to_know: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
common_options: peanut-free | extra herbs | nước chấm | no pork
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần gỏi cuốn tôm thịt.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of fresh spring rolls with shrimp and pork.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn goy kwun tom tit
what_it_is: Gỏi cuốn tôm thịt is a fresh rice-paper roll with shrimp, pork, herbs, lettuce, and noodles. Peanut-hoisin dip makes it nutty and rich, while nước chấm keeps it lighter.
how_to_enjoy: Eat the rolls cool, dipping each bite in peanut-hoisin or nước chấm depending on the shop. The rice paper should stay soft and the herbs should taste fresh.
how_locals_order: Order gỏi cuốn tôm thịt by the plate or by the roll, then choose the dip. Ask about peanuts before choosing peanut-hoisin if allergies matter.
worth_knowing: This is the classic fresh roll: shrimp, pork, herbs, noodles, and rice paper, a lighter counterpoint to fried spring rolls.
traveler_caution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.

at_a_glance: Nem cuốn is fresh nem rolls, usually with rice paper, herbs, noodles, pork or shrimp depending on the shop, and peanut-hoisin dip or nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip.
usually_includes: rice paper | fresh rolls, northern style | rice vermicelli | herbs | peanut sauce or nước chấm
good_to_know: If peanut-hoisin dip or nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip comes separately, start with a small dip; it can be salty, sweet, sour, and spicy at once.
common_options: peanut-free | extra herbs | nước chấm | no pork
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần nem cuốn.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of fresh rolls, northern style.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn nem kwun
what_it_is: Nem cuốn is a cool rice-paper roll with herbs, noodles, and pork or shrimp depending on the shop. Peanut-hoisin dip makes it rich; nước chấm makes it lighter and sharper.
how_to_enjoy: Eat nem cuốn fresh, before the herbs wilt and the rice paper dries. Dip each bite lightly so the roll stays clean and bright.
how_locals_order: Order nem cuốn by the plate or by the roll, then ask which dip comes with it. If peanuts are a problem, say no peanuts before the dip arrives.
worth_knowing: Across Vietnam, nem cuốn can overlap with fresh-roll language in different regions, so the filling and dip matter more than the English translation.

at_a_glance: Nem nướng cuốn is fresh rolls with grilled pork sausage, usually with nem nướng, herbs, pickles, rice paper, and a thick Nha Trang-style peanut-garlic dip.
usually_includes: rice paper | pork | rice vermicelli | herbs | thick Nha Trang-style peanut-garlic dip
good_to_know: May contain pork.
common_options: extra rice paper | no peanuts | no chili | extra herbs
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần nem nướng cuốn.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of grilled pork sausage rolls.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn nem noong kwun
what_it_is: Nem nướng cuốn is grilled pork sausage wrapped with rice paper, herbs, cucumber, pickles, noodles, and a thick peanut-garlic dip. It is smoky, crunchy, fresh, and rich at once.
how_to_enjoy: Build each roll with nem nướng, herbs, crunch, and noodles, then dip into the thick peanut-garlic dip. Use less dip at first; it can be sweet and rich.
how_locals_order: Order nem nướng cuốn when you want the roll-it-yourself version of grilled pork sausage. Ask for extra rice paper, no peanuts, or no chili before the platter arrives.
worth_knowing: Nha Trang-style nem nướng is famous for the dip and the crunchy bits inside the roll, not just the pork sausage.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Chả giò is Vietnamese fried spring rolls, usually with crisp shell, pork or mixed filling, lettuce, herbs, and fish sauce.
usually_includes: fried wrapper | fried spring rolls | vegetables | herbs | nước chấm
good_to_know: If nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip with sugar, garlic, and chili comes separately, start with a small dip; it can be salty, sweet, sour, and spicy at once.
common_options: extra lettuce | extra herbs | no chili | extra nước chấm
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần chả giò.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of fried spring rolls.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn chah yaw
what_it_is: Chả giò are southern Vietnamese fried spring rolls, usually pork or mixed filling in a crisp wrapper, served with lettuce, herbs, and nước chấm.
how_to_enjoy: Wrap a hot fried roll in lettuce or herbs, then dip in nước chấm. The greens cool the fried shell and keep each bite fresh.
how_locals_order: Order chả giò as a shared starter or alongside bún. Ask for no chili in the nước chấm, and use the lettuce and herbs instead of eating the rolls plain.
worth_knowing: In southern Vietnam, chả giò is the fried-roll word visitors need; in the north, you may see nem rán for a similar idea.

at_a_glance: Chả giò tôm thịt is fried spring rolls with shrimp and pork, usually with rice paper or wheat wrapper, herbs, lettuce, and nước chấm.
usually_includes: fried wrapper | shrimp and pork filling | lettuce | fresh herbs | nước chấm
good_to_know: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
common_options: extra lettuce | extra herbs | no chili | extra nước chấm
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần chả giò tôm thịt.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of fried spring rolls with shrimp and pork.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn chah yaw tom tit
what_it_is: Chả giò tôm thịt are fried spring rolls filled with shrimp and pork, served crisp with lettuce, herbs, and nước chấm.
how_to_enjoy: Wrap the crisp roll in lettuce or herbs, then dip lightly in nước chấm. The shrimp-pork filling is richer when the greens stay fresh.
how_locals_order: Order chả giò tôm thịt when you want the shrimp-and-pork fried roll. Ask for no chili in the nước chấm or extra lettuce before sharing.
worth_knowing: Tôm thịt means shrimp and pork, a useful filling phrase across rolls, dumplings, and noodle dishes.
traveler_caution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.

at_a_glance: Nem rán is northern fried spring rolls, usually with pork, glass noodles, wood ear, crisp wrapper, lettuce, and nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip with sugar, garlic, and chili.
usually_includes: fried wrapper | northern fried spring rolls | vegetables | herbs | nước chấm
good_to_know: Northern-style fried rolls often include pork, mushroom, and glass noodles; dip lightly so the crisp wrapper stays crisp.
common_options: extra herbs | extra lettuce | no chili | extra nước chấm
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần nem rán.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of northern fried spring rolls.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn nem rahn
what_it_is: Nem rán are northern fried spring rolls, often filled with pork, glass noodles, wood ear mushroom, and vegetables, then served with herbs and nước chấm.
how_to_enjoy: Wrap a piece in herbs or lettuce if served, then dip in nước chấm. Eat while crisp, before the fried wrapper softens.
how_locals_order: Order nem rán as the northern fried-roll name. Ask for no chili in the nước chấm and use the herbs to balance the fried shell.
worth_knowing: Nem rán and chả giò can refer to similar fried-roll territory, but the regional wording helps you read menus from north to south.

at_a_glance: Bì cuốn is fresh rolls with shredded pork skin, usually with rice paper, herbs, noodles, thính, and nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip with sugar, garlic, and chili.
usually_includes: rice paper | shredded pork skin | toasted rice powder | herbs | nước chấm
good_to_know: May contain pork.
common_options: nước chấm on the side | extra herbs | no pork | no chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bì cuốn.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of shredded pork skin rolls.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bee kwun
what_it_is: Bì cuốn are rice-paper rolls filled with shredded pork skin, toasted rice powder, herbs, noodles, and often nước chấm. The toasted rice powder gives the pork its nutty aroma.
how_to_enjoy: Dip lightly so the rice paper stays intact and the toasted-rice aroma of the bì remains clear. Eat soon, while the herbs are fresh.
how_locals_order: Order bì cuốn by the plate or roll. Ask for nước chấm on the side, no pork, or extra herbs before the rolls are served.
worth_knowing: Bì means shredded pork skin mixed with thính, toasted rice powder; it is much more aromatic than the English phrase suggests.
traveler_caution: May contain pork.

at_a_glance: Bò bía is thin fresh rolls with jicama and sausage, usually with egg, herbs, dried shrimp, and peanut-hoisin sauce.

good_to_know: If peanut-hoisin dip or nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip comes separately, start with a small dip; it can be salty, sweet, sour, and spicy at once.
common_options: no peanuts | no dried shrimp | extra herbs | less chili
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bò bía.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of jicama and sausage rolls.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn baw bee-ah
what_it_is: Bò bía is a soft rice-paper roll with jicama, Chinese sausage, egg, dried shrimp, herbs, and peanut-hoisin dip. It is sweet, savory, crunchy, and snacky.
how_to_enjoy: Dip each roll in peanut-hoisin and eat while the rice paper is still soft. Ask about peanuts or dried shrimp if allergies matter.
how_locals_order: Order bò bía as a snack by the roll or plate. Ask for no peanuts or no dried shrimp before the roll is made.
worth_knowing: At Vietnamese snack stalls, bò bía is not a beef roll; the usual flavor comes from jicama, sausage, egg, herbs, and peanut-hoisin dip.

at_a_glance: Chạo tôm is grilled shrimp paste on sugarcane, usually served with herbs, rice paper, noodles, and nước chấm.
usually_includes: shrimp paste | sugarcane | rice paper | fresh herbs | nước chấm
good_to_know: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
common_options: extra rice paper | extra herbs | no chili | extra nước chấm
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần chạo tôm.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of sugarcane shrimp.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn chow tom
what_it_is: Chạo tôm is springy shrimp paste wrapped around sugarcane and grilled. You pull off the shrimp, wrap it with herbs and rice paper if served, then dip for a sweet, smoky, seafood-rich bite.
how_to_enjoy: Slide the shrimp paste from the sugarcane, build a bite with herbs, noodles, and rice paper if provided, then dip lightly. The sugarcane gives aroma more than something to chew through.
how_locals_order: Order chạo tôm as a shared starter or roll-your-own plate. Ask for extra rice paper, extra herbs, or no chili in the nước chấm before the plate arrives.
worth_knowing: Chạo tôm is associated with central Vietnamese celebration food, especially Huế-style spreads where grilled, wrapped, and dipped bites matter.
traveler_caution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.

at_a_glance: Bò lá lốt is beef wrapped in betel leaves, usually with grilled aroma, herbs, rice paper, and nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip with sugar, garlic, and chili.
usually_includes: beef in betel leaves | herbs | rice paper optional | nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip with sugar, garlic, and chili
good_to_know: Rice paper may be served depending on the shop; if you want to wrap, ask for bánh tráng.
common_options: extra rice paper | extra herbs | no chili | extra nước chấm
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bò lá lốt.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of beef wrapped in betel leaves.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn baw lah loht
what_it_is: Bò lá lốt is seasoned beef wrapped in aromatic lá lốt leaves and grilled. It is often eaten with herbs, rice paper, noodles, and nước chấm so the smoky leaf perfumes the whole bite.
how_to_enjoy: Wrap a beef roll with herbs, noodles, and rice paper if served, then dip lightly in nước chấm. The lá lốt aroma should stay noticeable.
how_locals_order: Order bò lá lốt as a shared grilled snack. Ask for extra rice paper or herbs if you want to eat it the local wrap-and-dip way.
worth_knowing: In Vietnam, lá lốt is piper lolot, often called wild betel leaf; it gives the beef a peppery herbal smell travelers remember.

at_a_glance: Bánh xèo is a crisp turmeric-rice pancake eaten by tearing pieces into rice paper or lettuce with herbs, then dipping in nước chấm.
usually_includes: rice flour batter | pork and shrimp | bean sprouts | rice paper or lettuce | fresh herbs and nước chấm
good_to_know: Fresh herbs are part of the flavor, not a garnish. Skip chili if you want the nước chấm milder.
common_options: extra rice paper | extra herbs | no chili | extra nước chấm
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh xèo.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of crispy Vietnamese pancake.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn say-oh
what_it_is: Bánh xèo is a sizzling turmeric-rice pancake folded around pork, shrimp, bean sprouts, and herbs. The local fun is not fork-and-knife pancake eating: you tear it, wrap it with rice paper or lettuce and herbs, then dip in nước chấm.
how_to_enjoy: Tear off a crisp piece, tuck it into rice paper or lettuce with herbs, roll or fold it, then dip lightly in nước chấm. The herbs and wrapper are part of the dish, not decoration.
how_locals_order: Order bánh xèo expecting a hands-on wrap-and-dip plate. Ask for extra bánh tráng or herbs if the table is sharing, and say no chili in the nước chấm before dipping starts.
worth_knowing: Bánh xèo changes by region, but the eating ritual is the traveler key: crisp pancake, fresh herbs, rice paper or lettuce, and bright fish-sauce dip in one bite.

at_a_glance: Bánh khọt is mini crispy turmeric pancakes, usually with shrimp, coconut richness, herbs, and fish sauce.
usually_includes: rice flour batter | coconut milk | shrimp | lettuce or rice paper | herbs and nước chấm
good_to_know: If nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip with sugar, garlic, and chili comes separately, start with a small dip; it can be salty, sweet, sour, and spicy at once.
common_options: extra rice paper | extra herbs | no chili | extra nước chấm
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh khọt.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of mini savory coconut pancakes.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn kawt
what_it_is: Bánh khọt are tiny turmeric-coconut rice pancakes, often topped with shrimp and eaten with herbs, lettuce or rice paper, and nước chấm.
how_to_enjoy: Wrap each hot mini pancake in lettuce, herbs, or rice paper if served, then dip in nước chấm. Eat while the edges are still crisp.
how_locals_order: Order bánh khọt for sharing while hot. Ask for extra herbs, extra bánh tráng, or no chili in the nước chấm before the tray arrives.
worth_knowing: Bánh khọt is strongly linked with Vũng Tàu and southern coastal snacking, where crisp edges, shrimp, coconut richness, and herbs do the work.

at_a_glance: Bánh căn is small griddled rice cakes, usually with quail egg or seafood, herbs, and nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip with sugar, garlic, and chili.
usually_includes: rice batter | quail egg or seafood | scallions | herbs | nước chấm
good_to_know: Quail egg, shrimp, or pork may be cooked into the little cakes; ask before ordering if you need a plain or vegetarian set.
common_options: no chili | ask about seafood | extra herbs | extra nước chấm
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh căn.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of mini crispy rice pancakes.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn kan
what_it_is: Bánh căn are small south-central rice pancakes cooked in clay molds, often with quail egg, seafood, scallions, and nước chấm. They are softer and more custardy than bánh khọt.
how_to_enjoy: Dip the small cakes into nước chấm while they are warm, adding herbs and pickles if served. Ask about egg or seafood before ordering if either matters.
how_locals_order: Order bánh căn by portion size and topping. Ask for no chili in the nước chấm or a seafood-free version before the cakes go into the molds.
worth_knowing: Bánh căn is a south-central snack, especially around Đà Lạt, Nha Trang, and Phan Rang, where tiny clay-mold pancakes become a whole meal of dips and herbs.

english_translation: Steamed rice cakes with shrimp topping
at_a_glance: Tiny steamed rice cakes from central Vietnam, topped with shrimp floss, scallion oil, and fish sauce for spoon-by-spoon bites.
usually_includes: steamed rice cakes | shrimp topping | scallion oil | fried shallots | nước chấm
good_to_know: If you avoid shrimp, ask whether the shrimp topping or nước mắm can be left off.
common_options: extra nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip with sugar, garlic, and chili | more herbs | no chili | share size
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh bèo.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of steamed rice cakes with shrimp topping.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn beh-oh
what_it_is: Bánh bèo comes in small dishes or saucers: soft rice batter steamed until tender, then finished with savory shrimp crumbs, crispy bits, scallion oil, and nước mắm.
how_to_enjoy: Add a little fish sauce to each cup and use the spoon to release the cake from the dish. The fun is in eating several small, delicate bites rather than one big plate.
how_locals_order: Order bánh bèo as small steamed rice cakes in little cups or shallow dishes, usually several at a time. Spoon nước chấm lightly so the shrimp topping and fried shallots stay clear.
worth_knowing: This is a signature of Huế and central Vietnamese snack culture, where careful textures and tiny portions can carry a surprising amount of flavor.
traveler_caution: Often topped with shrimp and nước mắm.

english_translation: Clear tapioca dumplings with shrimp and pork
at_a_glance: Bánh bột lọc is translucent tapioca dumplings, usually with shrimp and pork, chewy wrapper, banana leaf, and fish sauce.
usually_includes: tapioca wrapper | shrimp | pork | banana leaf optional | nước chấm
good_to_know: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
common_options: no chili | ask about shrimp | extra nước chấm | pack to go
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh bột lọc.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of clear tapioca dumplings with shrimp and pork.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn boht lawk
what_it_is: Bánh bột lọc are chewy translucent tapioca dumplings, often filled with shrimp and pork, sometimes wrapped in banana leaf, and eaten with nước chấm.
how_to_enjoy: Peel the banana leaf if needed, then spoon nước chấm lightly over the dumplings. The pleasure is the chewy wrapper against salty shrimp and pork.
how_locals_order: Order bánh bột lọc when you want a chewy Huế-style snack. Ask if it contains shrimp or pork before ordering, and request no chili in the nước chấm if needed.
worth_knowing: This central Vietnamese dumpling is loved for texture; the wrapper should be pleasantly chewy, not just a container.
traveler_caution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.

at_a_glance: Bánh nậm is flat steamed rice dumplings in banana leaf, usually with shrimp-pork topping and fish sauce.
usually_includes: rice flour sheet | banana leaf | shrimp or pork topping | scallion oil | nước chấm
good_to_know: If nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip with sugar, garlic, and chili comes separately, start with a small dip; it can be salty, sweet, sour, and spicy at once.
common_options: no chili | ask about shrimp | ask about pork | extra nước chấm
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh nậm.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of flat steamed rice dumplings.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn nahm
what_it_is: Bánh nậm is a flat Huế rice-flour dumpling steamed in banana leaf, usually with minced shrimp or pork scattered across the soft rice sheet.
how_to_enjoy: Open the banana leaf, spoon on a little nước chấm, and eat the soft rice sheet gently so the topping stays in each bite.
how_locals_order: Order bánh nậm by portion, often several pieces at a time. Ask about shrimp or pork if you avoid either, and say no chili before nước chấm is added.
worth_knowing: Bánh nậm is part of Huế’s delicate bánh culture, where small steamed cakes show off texture and careful dipping.

at_a_glance: Bánh cuốn is steamed rice rolls, usually with minced pork, wood ear mushroom, fried shallot, herbs, and nước chấm.
usually_includes: steamed rice rolls | pork and mushroom filling | fried shallots | herbs | nước chấm
good_to_know: Bánh cuốn is often a breakfast or snack plate with chả lụa on the side. Spoon nước chấm gradually so the rice sheets stay silky.
common_options: nước chấm on the side | extra fried shallots | extra herbs | no pork
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh cuốn.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of steamed rice rolls.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn kwun
what_it_is: Bánh cuốn are delicate steamed rice sheets rolled around minced pork and wood ear mushroom, topped with fried shallots and eaten with herbs, chả, and nước chấm.
how_to_enjoy: Spoon nước chấm over the rice rolls gradually, then add herbs and fried shallots to each bite. The sheets are soft, so a light hand keeps them silky.
how_locals_order: Order bánh cuốn as a breakfast or snack plate, often with chả lụa on the side. Ask for no pork or nước chấm riêng before the plate is finished.
worth_knowing: A good bánh cuốn shop often steams the rice sheets fresh, which is why the rolls feel soft and almost translucent.

at_a_glance: Bánh tráng nướng is grilled rice paper “pizza”, usually with egg, scallion, dried shrimp or sausage, chili sauce, and crackle.
usually_includes: grilled rice paper | egg or toppings | scallions | chili sauce
good_to_know: Often called “Vietnamese pizza,” but expect rice paper, egg, dried shrimp or sausage, scallions, and chili rather than cheese-heavy pizza.
common_options: no chili | extra egg | no dried shrimp | share size
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh tráng nướng.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of grilled rice paper, Vietnamese pizza.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn chang noong
what_it_is: Bánh tráng nướng is grilled rice paper cooked until crisp with egg, scallions, dried shrimp or sausage, chili, and mayonnaise-style or savory toppings. It is often nicknamed Vietnamese pizza.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it hot before the rice paper loses its crackle. Say no chili before the vendor sauces the top, because the spice gets baked into the snack.
how_locals_order: Order bánh tráng nướng by topping if the stall offers choices. Ask for no chili, no dried shrimp, or extra egg before it hits the grill.
worth_knowing: This is a street-snack texture dish: thin rice paper turns brittle and smoky, while egg and toppings make it savory enough to share.

at_a_glance: Bánh tráng trộn is tossed rice paper salad, usually with shredded rice paper, green mango, herbs, quail egg, dried beef or shrimp, and chili.
usually_includes: rice paper strips | green mango | herbs | chili dressing | snack toppings
good_to_know: This snack often includes dried shrimp, quail egg, peanuts, chili, and tart tamarind dressing; ask no chili early if heat matters.
common_options: less spicy | no peanuts | no dried shrimp | extra mango
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bánh tráng trộn.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of mixed rice paper salad.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn bahn chang chohn
what_it_is: Bánh tráng trộn is mixed rice-paper salad tossed with green mango, herbs, chili, quail egg, dried beef or shrimp, peanuts, and tangy seasoning.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it soon after mixing, while the rice paper is chewy rather than soggy. Ask for less chili or no peanuts before the vendor tosses the bag or bowl.
how_locals_order: Order bánh tráng trộn as a made-to-order snack. Say ít cay, không đậu phộng, or no dried shrimp before everything is mixed.
worth_knowing: The fun is texture: chewy rice paper, sour mango, chili heat, herbs, and crunchy toppings all changing as it sits.

english_translation: Lotus stem salad with shrimp and pork
at_a_glance: Gỏi ngó sen tôm thịt is lotus-stem salad with shrimp and pork, usually with crisp lotus stems, herbs, peanuts, and sweet-tart dressing.
usually_includes: lotus stem | shrimp and pork | fresh herbs | peanuts | fish-sauce lime dressing
good_to_know: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
common_options: no peanuts | no pork | less spicy | extra herbs
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần gỏi ngó sen tôm thịt.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of lotus stem salad with shrimp and pork.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn goy ngoh sen tom tit
what_it_is: Gỏi ngó sen tôm thịt is lotus-stem salad with shrimp, pork, herbs, peanuts, and a bright fish-sauce-lime dressing. The lotus stems give it a juicy crunch.
how_to_enjoy: Toss lightly so the lotus stems stay crisp, then eat with shrimp, pork, herbs, and peanuts in each bite. Add chili only if you want heat over the clean crunch.
how_locals_order: Order gỏi ngó sen tôm thịt as a shared salad. Ask for no peanuts, no pork, or less chili before it is dressed.
worth_knowing: In Vietnamese salads, lotus stem is the signature texture here; it is refreshing, crisp, and very different from leafy salad.
traveler_caution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.

at_a_glance: Gỏi xoài is green mango salad, usually with herbs, peanuts, dried shrimp or seafood, and chili-fish sauce dressing.
usually_includes: green mango | herbs | peanuts | dried shrimp optional | fish-sauce-lime dressing
good_to_know: Ask about dried shrimp, dried beef, peanuts, and chili before it is tossed; those small toppings change the whole salad.
common_options: less spicy | no peanuts | no dried shrimp | extra herbs
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần gỏi xoài.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of green mango salad.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn goy swai
what_it_is: Gỏi xoài is green mango salad, usually tossed with herbs, peanuts, dried shrimp or beef jerky depending on the shop, and fish-sauce-lime dressing. It is crisp, tart, sweet, salty, and lively.
how_to_enjoy: Toss before eating so the dressing reaches the mango, then taste before adding chili. Ask about dried shrimp or beef jerky if you avoid either.
how_locals_order: Order gỏi xoài as a snack or shared salad. Say ít cay, không đậu phộng, or no dried shrimp before it is tossed.
worth_knowing: Green mango in Vietnam is firm and sour, which is why the dressing can be sweet, salty, spicy, and still feel refreshing.

at_a_glance: Gỏi đu đủ is green papaya salad, usually with herbs, peanuts, dried beef or shrimp, and tart fish sauce dressing.
usually_includes: green papaya | herbs | peanuts | fish-sauce-lime dressing | dried beef or shrimp optional
good_to_know: Ask for không cay if you want Gỏi đu đủ without added chili.
common_options: less spicy | no peanuts | no dried beef | extra herbs
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần gỏi đu đủ.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of green papaya salad.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn goy doo doo
what_it_is: Gỏi đu đủ is green papaya salad, usually shredded and tossed with herbs, peanuts, chili, and fish-sauce-lime dressing. It should be crunchy, sour, sweet, salty, and a little spicy.
how_to_enjoy: Toss before eating so the dressing reaches the papaya, then taste before adding chili. Ask about dried beef or shrimp if you are avoiding either.
how_locals_order: Order gỏi đu đủ as a snack or shared salad. Say ít cay, không đậu phộng, or no dried beef before it is tossed.
worth_knowing: In Vietnamese snack salads, green papaya is crisp and mild; the dressing and toppings provide most of the flavor.

at_a_glance: Gỏi gà is chicken salad, usually with cabbage, rau răm, onion, peanuts, and lime-fish sauce dressing.
usually_includes: shredded chicken | cabbage or herbs | onion | peanuts | fish-sauce lime dressing
good_to_know: Chicken salad often uses fish sauce, rau răm, onion, and peanuts; the herb bite is part of the dish.
common_options: no peanuts | less onion | less spicy | extra herbs
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần gỏi gà.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of Vietnamese chicken salad.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn goy gah
what_it_is: Gỏi gà is shredded chicken salad with cabbage or banana blossom, rau răm, onion, peanuts, fried shallots, and fish-sauce-lime dressing.
how_to_enjoy: Toss lightly so the shredded chicken picks up herbs and dressing without turning soggy. Peanuts and fried shallots should add crunch at the end.
how_locals_order: Order gỏi gà as a shared salad or light meal. Ask for no peanuts, less onion, or less chili before it is tossed.
worth_knowing: Rau răm gives many Vietnamese chicken salads their peppery, herbal lift; it is part of the identity, not a garnish.

english_translation: Green papaya salad with dried beef
at_a_glance: Nộm bò khô is dried beef salad, usually with green papaya, herbs, peanuts, and tangy dressing.
usually_includes: green papaya | dried beef | peanuts | herbs | fish-sauce-lime dressing
good_to_know: This Hanoi-style snack is about dried beef, green papaya, herbs, peanuts, and chili. Ask ít cay or không đậu phộng before mixing.
common_options: less spicy | no peanuts | extra dried beef | extra herbs
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần nộm bò khô.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of green papaya salad with dried beef.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn nohm baw koh
what_it_is: Nộm bò khô is northern-style green papaya salad with dried beef, herbs, peanuts, and a tart-sweet dressing. It is chewy, crunchy, tangy, and snacky.
how_to_enjoy: Mix the dried beef through the papaya so each bite gets chew, crunch, herbs, and dressing. Ask for less chili before it is tossed.
how_locals_order: Order nộm bò khô as a snack plate. Say không đậu phộng or ít cay before the vendor adds peanuts and chili.
worth_knowing: Nộm is the northern word travelers often see for salad; this one is more street-snack than leafy salad.

at_a_glance: Súp cua is a thick crab soup with egg ribbons, pepper, cilantro, and sometimes corn or asparagus. It is warm, silky, and snack-sized.
usually_includes: crab soup | egg ribbons | corn or asparagus | cilantro | pepper
good_to_know: A little pepper or chili can wake up the bowl, but the texture should stay silky and crab-sweet.
common_options: no pepper | no chili oil | extra quail egg | ask about crab
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô súp cua.
quick_say_english: I’d like one bowl of crab soup.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht toh soop koo-ah
what_it_is: Súp cua is thick crab soup with egg ribbons, crab meat, mushrooms or quail egg, cilantro, and black pepper. It is silky, warming, and often sold as a small snack bowl.
how_to_enjoy: Stir gently, add pepper or chili oil only after tasting, and eat while hot so the egg ribbons and crab stay silky.
how_locals_order: Order súp cua by bowl size, then ask for no pepper or no chili oil if you want it gentle. Ask about crab or quail egg if allergies matter.
worth_knowing: This is a comfort snack rather than a seafood feast; the texture should be thick and spoonable.
traveler_caution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.

at_a_glance: Cá viên chiên is fried fish balls, usually with skewers, chili sauce, and lime-pepper salt dip or ginger fish sauce.
usually_includes: fish balls | fried edges | skewers optional | chili dip | cucumber optional
good_to_know: Ask for không cay if you want Cá viên chiên without added chili.
common_options: no chili | mixed skewers | lime-pepper salt | share size
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cá viên chiên.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of fried fish balls.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kah vee-en chee-en
what_it_is: Cá viên chiên are fried fish balls, often skewered or served in a basket with chili dip, cucumber, and sometimes lime-pepper salt. They are a casual street snack.
how_to_enjoy: Eat them hot while the outside is springy-crisp, then dip lightly in chili or lime-pepper salt. Ask for no chili if you want the fish-cake sweetness plain.
how_locals_order: Order cá viên chiên by choosing skewers or asking for a mixed fried snack plate. Say không cay before the vendor adds chili dip.
worth_knowing: This is school-snack and street-cart territory in Vietnam: quick, fun, and more about texture than a formal meal.

at_a_glance: Khoai lang chiên is fried sweet potato with a crisp outside and soft orange or yellow center, often eaten as a simple street snack.
usually_includes: sweet potato | light batter or crisp edges | salt or sugar | hot oil frying
good_to_know: This is snack food, not a saucy dish. Eat it hot when the outside is crisp and the sweet potato center is still soft.
common_options: no chili | less salt | pack to go | share size
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần khoai lang chiên.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of fried sweet potato.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kwai lahng chee-en
what_it_is: Khoai lang chiên is fried sweet potato, usually crisp outside and soft-sweet inside, sometimes with salt, sesame, or a light batter depending on the stall.
how_to_enjoy: Eat it hot while the outside is crisp and the center is sweet. Ask for no chili powder if you want a simple sweet-salty snack.
how_locals_order: Order khoai lang chiên as a street snack or side. Ask for no chili, less salt, or pack to go before the batch is bagged.
worth_knowing: Vietnamese fried sweet potato can be a roadside snack rather than dessert; the pleasure is the hot contrast of crisp edge and soft center.

at_a_glance: Khoai tây chiên is fried potatoes: salty, crisp, familiar, and often ordered as a snack or side at cafés and casual restaurants.
usually_includes: potatoes | salt | crisp fried edges | ketchup or chili sauce if served
good_to_know: This is the familiar fries order. It is useful for picky eaters, kids, or a quick snack, but it is not where the menu shows its deepest Vietnamese flavor.
common_options: no chili | less salt | ketchup | pack to go
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần khoai tây chiên.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of french fries.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kwai tay chee-en
what_it_is: Khoai tây chiên are fries, usually served hot with salt, chili powder, ketchup, or mayonnaise-style dip depending on the stall or cafe.
how_to_enjoy: Eat while crisp and ask for chili separately if you want a mild order. This is familiar, but Vietnamese stalls may season more boldly than expected.
how_locals_order: Order khoai tây chiên as a side or snack. Ask không ớt, ít muối, or mang đi before the fries are packed.
worth_knowing: This is not uniquely Vietnamese, but it appears on cafe, snack, and beer-food menus where seasoning and dips vary by shop.

at_a_glance: Cá kho tộ is fish simmered in a clay pot with fish sauce, caramelized sugar, pepper, and sometimes pork fat until the fish-sauce caramel braise turns dark and glossy.
usually_includes: fish | fish sauce caramel | black pepper | clay pot | rice on the side
good_to_know: The clay-pot glaze is a fish-sauce caramel: salty, sweet, peppery, and concentrated. Eat it with plain rice and ask about bones if you prefer easier pieces.
common_options: extra rice | ask about bones | less pepper | share clay pot
quick_say_vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần cá kho tộ.
quick_say_english: I’d like one order of caramelized fish in clay pot.
quick_say_sound_out: chaw toy moht fuhn kah kaw toh
what_it_is: Cá kho tộ is fish braised in a clay pot with fish sauce, caramelized sugar, black pepper, and sometimes pork fat until the fish-sauce caramel braise is glossy and intense.

traveler_caution: May contain pork.
